- **Most of a compounder's wealth arrives late: Buffett's net worth at 50 was one-third of 1% of what it is today, so keep the engine running as long as possible.** Over 99% of Buffett's wealth came after age 50. Pabrai says 23 of his own 30-year game have passed and most of the money comes at the end, so he has decided not to stop at 60 but to keep going to 80 or 85. _[Warren Buffett]_ — [2017-12-22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z74NaYRyMJo)

### Moats & business quality (3)

- **Float, especially permanent float that will never be redeemed, lets you control far more assets than you pay for.** In 1967 Blue Chip had ~$50M equity, ~$100M of float (perhaps half never to be redeemed) and traded at $40M; the group took 25M of that float to buy See's Candies in 1972 and another 25M for Wesco in 1973. _[Blue Chip Stamps, See's Candies, Wesco Financial]_ — [2017-06-07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bLjoL5zhBxA)
- **Commodity businesses can have moats: the lowest-cost producer with no leverage, bought at a low valuation, is money in the bank.** Saudi oil at $2 a barrel sold at $60, or Pilbara iron ore scooped from the surface, are great businesses; avoid high-cost producers like $60-plus North Sea oil even when cheap. His 9x Indian holding is the lowest-cost producer in its market, an enduring tailwind. _[Rain Industries]_ — [2017-11-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_1aGen3q2_g)
- **With no leverage you can hold through any crash, so seek businesses like Google and Maotai that crank out cash without debt.** If North Korea launched missiles the market might fall 50-70%, but Maotai consumption would normalize and Stanford real estate would be unaffected long term; you must be positioned to take advantage of such events, never to go to zero, because any number multiplied by zero is zero. _[Kweichow Moutai, Google, John Arrillaga]_ — [2017-12-22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z74NaYRyMJo)

### Management & capital allocation (1)

- **He works alone with no analysts because a team creates pressure to act; instead he wants the wisdom of crowds, a million analysts sending him ideas.** A stranger in Canada sent him an elegant write-up on an Indian stock trading at one-tenth of value; after three hours of fact-checking he invested the maximum allowed ($20 million, under 10% of a sub-$200 million company) and it rose 10x in two and a half years. A smart hired analyst would bring ideas outside his circle and he would eventually feel obliged to buy one. — [2017-12-22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z74NaYRyMJo)

### Markets, cycles & macro (3)

- **Never make investment decisions based on who is in office; US presidents have very little power and the system tends toward inaction.** Where Daehan Flour or Frontline trade has nothing to do with who is in power; spending time on the nuances of President Trump is entertaining but will not help your net worth. — [2017-06-07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bLjoL5zhBxA)
- **The commandments of Buffett, Munger and Graham are: thou shall not fixate on macro, forecast recessions, short anything, or hedge.** Asked about a flat yield curve and Black Swan positions, he says it is hard enough to figure out one business over two or three years; instead find long positions where the economy is irrelevant. _[Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger, Ben Graham]_ — [2017-11-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_1aGen3q2_g)
- **Auction-driven markets swing far wider than intrinsic value, which is why a stock-picker can beat passive investing and why more indexing is good news for stock pickers.** A Boston townhouse appraised daily by a sensible realtor would range 5% in a year, but listed on the NYSE it would trade from $700k to $1.3 million. Markets paint with a wide brush - a company like Axalta gets 'taken out back and shot' for one bad quarter. 'The more drones in the market, the better off we are.' _[Axalta, Amazon]_ — [2017-11-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_1aGen3q2_g)

### Stock case studies (3)

- **Ride sharing and autonomy are tailwinds for auto and especially tire companies because cheaper mobility raises miles driven.** Full level-five autonomy is 10-20 years away, but with Fiat Chrysler bought at roughly a P/E of one on 2018-19 earnings he doesn't care about 2025-30; a tipster sent him an obscure tire company at 2.5x earnings that trades by appointment, and he has nibbled ~$4 million so far in a $560M fund. _[Fiat Chrysler, Uber]_ — [2017-06-07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bLjoL5zhBxA)
- **Stewart Enterprises at a P/E of 2 in 2002 shows you can find recession-proof bets: you earn the whole price back in two years as long as humans keep dying.** Found on Value Line's lowest-P/E list; funeral homes have recurring franchise-like demand, no price shopping, and no HBS grads rushing in to compete. Yet the stock fell with everything after 9/11 when its prospects if anything improved - proof that auction-driven markets are inefficient. Service Corp later traded at $37 and 15-17x earnings. _[Stewart Enterprises, Service Corp International, Value Line, United Airlines]_ — [2017-11-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_1aGen3q2_g)
- **He bought GM warrants in 2012 rather than LEAPs because they had seven years of duration and distressed-era terms dictated by the US Treasury.** US LEAPs max out at two years; the GM warrants could be handed to the company for stock at any time and were an instrument GM would never issue except under bankruptcy-era distress, so they were unusually attractive. _[General Motors]_ — [2017-12-22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z74NaYRyMJo)

### Geographies: India, China, Turkey, Japan, US (5)

- **Cheapness gets over a lot of negatives, such as Japanese governance issues and hoarded cash.** He and Guy Spier screened Japanese net-nets via the Japan Company Handbook and Capital IQ; a basket of 10-20 Japanese net-nets needs maybe 30 minutes per company with small bet sizes. _[Guy Spier, Japan Company Handbook]_ — [2017-06-07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bLjoL5zhBxA)
- **South Korea in 2017 is one of the cheapest markets in the world, and Korean preferreds trading at a third to a half of the common are an irrational anomaly.** The preferreds are economically identical to the common except for voting rights (Google's two classes differ by only 2%), but Koreans view them with disdain because they were issued in the crisis bailouts; he suggests a basket of Korean preferreds such as Hyundai Motor preferred and also finds smaller-cap India relatively cheap. _[Hyundai Motor, Google]_ — [2017-06-07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bLjoL5zhBxA)
- **It doesn't matter how good a fisherman you are if you're not fishing where the fish are - so he pivoted from the US to India, which went from 0% to 45% of the portfolio in three years.** For nearly two years he has found little to buy at half-off in the US; US-domiciled companies are now under 13% of the $840 million portfolio. US listed companies have fallen from about 8,000 to under 3,700 while the brain cells picking through them keep rising, producing pricing to perfection. The one recent US anomaly was the airlines, bought 14-15 months earlier, a quarter before Berkshire. _[Pabrai Investment Funds, Airlines, Berkshire Hathaway]_ — [2017-11-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_1aGen3q2_g)
- **His India process is to fly in every six to eight weeks and meet 10-15 companies a week regardless of industry, earnings or multiple, purely to learn.** Being Indian, knowing the language and running a foundation there are natural advantages, and an outsider's bird's-eye view plus decades of mental models lets him see mispricings locals miss. India is 'fish in a barrel' even if the water hasn't been drained. — [2017-11-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_1aGen3q2_g)
- **Fish where the fish are: the US has shrunk from 8,000 to under 3,700 public companies while brainpower chasing them has exploded, whereas India has 5,000 listed companies, 4,000 of them followed by nobody.** In the last two or three years he has found almost nothing in the US, where physics PhDs join hedge funds instead of NASA and mispricing shrinks; India offers a faster-growing economy and huge tailwinds, and he sees China's standard of living as nearly doubled between his 2008 and 2017 visits. — [2017-12-22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z74NaYRyMJo)

### Psychology & temperament (7)

- **Great results come with serious pain: none of this was painless, and one must be able to sit through huge drawdowns.** In 1972 Wheeler Munger had 94% in two stocks (61% Blue Chip, 23% New America Fund); the partnership fell about 53% over 1973-74 even though the underlying assets were cheap and controlled, and Munger liquidated in 1975 distributing the stock and telling investors to hold. New America Fund later went from under $4 to $100 a unit in 1986. _[Wheeler Munger Partnership, Blue Chip Stamps, New America Fund, Daily Journal]_ — [2017-06-07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bLjoL5zhBxA)
- **Investing is an activity for a person of leisure; patience is like a law of physics in investing and hyperactivity does not jive with a great track record.** He suggests millennials get the hyperactivity out of their system with a day job such as a fast-moving start-up, keeping investing as a second bucket of reading and waiting; he admits he has not practiced enough patience himself and gives such talks partly to pound the idea into his own head. — [2017-06-07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bLjoL5zhBxA)
- **The business requires combining extreme patience with extreme decisiveness: do nothing for long periods, then act in size when the opportunity is obvious.** He believes these traits are partly genetic predisposition that can be built upon but not fully reprogrammed. — [2017-06-07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bLjoL5zhBxA)
- **Extreme success usually comes from taking a simple idea and pursuing it with fanatical intensity, not from high-horsepower ideas.** He opens and closes with the Einstein-attributed quote 'take a simple idea and take it seriously'; Buffett got rich on commonly known facts and commonly known math, applied obsessively from age 11 to 87. _[Warren Buffett]_ — [2017-11-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_1aGen3q2_g)
- **Managers should ignore redemptions, volatility and cash drag and focus on doing the best job; he has never been concerned about LPs leaving.** Only twice in 18 years has he called an investor to discourage a redemption (both institutions, both left anyway). If every LP left he would happily compound his own capital. Sitting on cash after raising the new India Focus Fund is irrelevant - it can take three to five years to put a fortune to work in stocks. _[Pabrai Investment Funds, India Focus Fund]_ — [2017-11-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_1aGen3q2_g)
- **Stop losses are stupid for a value investor because auction-driven markets fluctuate without regard to underlying value, and those fluctuations are the source of opportunity.** Indian TV pundits give a target and stop loss for every stock; the market prices Amazon at $1,200 to the cent when even Bezos cannot forecast its cash flows. He bought Maotai at about 170 RMB, it fell to 150 right after, and a stop loss would have taken him out. He uses a Beijing house analogy: a house quoted every six seconds would swing wildly with no change in the asset. _[Kweichow Moutai, Amazon, Jeff Bezos]_ — [2017-12-22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z74NaYRyMJo)
- **The two key traits of a value investor are patience (enjoy watching paint dry) and circle of competence; the test for understanding is that if you have any doubt, you do not understand it.** You must understand a business as well as the CEO, otherwise pass, put it in the too-hard file, or study until there is no doubt. Buffett told him he can only judge 4 of 100 people as really good and 4 as really bad and ignores the other 92; with 50,000 public companies you need only three or four to get rich. _[Warren Buffett]_ — [2017-12-22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z74NaYRyMJo)

### Buffett & Munger lessons (6)

- **Charlie Munger read Barron's for fifty years, acted on exactly one tip, and turned $10 million into roughly $500 million in fifteen years.** In 2002 he put $10M into Tenneco bonds and stock at 35 cents on the dollar, sold two years later for ~$80M, then gave the $80M to Li Lu, which has grown six or seven times; two actions in fifteen years produced a 50x. _[Tenneco, Li Lu, Charlie Munger]_ — [2017-06-07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bLjoL5zhBxA)
- **Buffett treats stock hunting like the kid collecting discarded winning tickets at Aksarben racetrack, and you cannot take Aksarben out of the kid.** In 1951 Buffett went through all 20,000 pages of Moody's Manuals twice and found things like Western Insurance earning $29 a share with $135 book value trading between $3 and $13; in 2011 Pabrai found the Japan Company Handbook on Buffett's desk, and in 2006 Buffett put $100M of personal money into 20 Korean stocks such as Daehan Flour at one third of liquidation value. _[Warren Buffett, Western Insurance, Japan Company Handbook, Daehan Flour Mills]_ — [2017-06-07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bLjoL5zhBxA)
- **Buffett's teenage Wilson Coin Operated Company is one of the most important business lessons: a capital-light business with return on capital higher than almost any American business.** In 1941 the 11-year-old Buffett read '1000 Ways to Make $1000' and declared he'd be a millionaire by 35 - he needed seed capital for his compounding engine. Buffett and Don Danley bought broken pinball machines for $15-30, fixed them, placed them free in DC barbershops with a 50/50 split; a $25 machine returned $2.50 a week. By 16-17 Buffett had about $9,000 saved and told his father to give his college money to his sisters. _[Warren Buffett, Don Danley, Wilson Coin Operated Company]_ — [2017-11-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_1aGen3q2_g)
- **Munger's 70-80x in 15 years came from a 'two-step slingshot': one 8x stock in 2002, then handing the proceeds to Li Lu - and he swung only once out of 25,000 Barron's tips.** Charlie read Barron's for 50 years, acted on one article (Tenneco), turned $10 million into $80 million, and picked one money manager in 94 years; that $80 million is likely $500-700 million now. Munger told him 'it only happened once in my life'. His own recurring mistakes: putting out a thimble when it's raining gold, and selling too early; he rereads Poor Charlie's Almanack every year. _[Charlie Munger, Li Lu, Tenneco, Daily Journal, Poor Charlie's Almanack]_ — [2017-11-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_1aGen3q2_g)
- **Buffett's success came from combining a seed-capital engine with an early, fanatical understanding of compounding.** At 11 in 1941 Buffett read '1000 Ways to Make $1000' and declared he would be a millionaire by 35; by 1965 he was worth $8-9 million. As a teenager he ran the Wilson Coin Operated Machine Company with Don Danley, placing 25 pinball machines in DC barbershops at $15 per machine that paid back in about six weeks, and rented a repaired Rolls-Royce for $100 a weekend. _[Warren Buffett, Don Danley, Wilson Coin Operated Machine Company]_ — [2017-12-22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z74NaYRyMJo)
- **Buffett kept changing his method while never changing his focus on compounding; the shift from fair businesses at good prices to good businesses at fair prices came only in his mid-50s.** He distinguishes understanding compounding (Buffett at 11) from understanding how to compound (Graham at 20), and notes the Munger-influenced quality shift happened when Buffett was 50-60, showing he continuously looks to improve. _[Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger, Ben Graham]_ — [2017-12-22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z74NaYRyMJo)

### Mistakes & lessons learned (6)

- **Selling Frontline at liquidation value was a mistake: he missed the supply-cycle upside and the stock eventually went 200 to one.** VLCCs take two or three years to build and get scrapped when rates hit $10K, so when demand returned rates went to a quarter million a day; like Class A office towers, the shipping cycle is driven by lemming-like ordering with long lead times. _[Frontline]_ — [2017-06-07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bLjoL5zhBxA)
- **The key to doing well in investing is inactivity; the single biggest mistake he has made historically is being too active.** Small team size is an advantage because it takes longer to get through ideas, which reduces activity. Being a part-time investor (as he was from 1995-99, and as his oncologist friend is) is an advantage because there is less reason to act. — [2017-11-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_1aGen3q2_g)
- **The Kelly Formula section of The Dhandho Investor was a mistake and should be ignored, because Kelly only works with a huge number of repeated bets with known odds.** In the stock market you rarely get repeated bets with well-known odds. He has never put more than 10% of assets into a single stock at purchase and prefers a '10 by 10' portfolio; research shows going from 10-15 stocks to 40 adds little diversification but costs a lot of performance. _[The Dhandho Investor]_ — [2017-11-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_1aGen3q2_g)
- **Buying an insurance company for its float was a mistake; the delusions about the wonders of float have been washed away.** He bought the insurer about three years earlier, found it a difficult business, and has agreed to sell it; he won't enter insurance again in this lifetime but would enter funeral services at one times earnings. — [2017-11-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_1aGen3q2_g)
- **Insurance is a structurally difficult business where your dumbest competitor sets your price and you do not know your product's cost for 5-10 years; he is exiting it for good.** After three years owning an insurance company he is selling it, having learned that policyholders treat premiums like a tax and shop for the cheapest, that inflation raises future claims paid in future dollars, and that Buffett made it work only because he is an incredible manager. He contrasts it with Maotai, which sells an 800 RMB bottle at a tiny cost, 'a license to print money'. _[Kweichow Moutai, Warren Buffett]_ — [2017-12-22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z74NaYRyMJo)
- **The number one reason investments fail is leverage; Delta Financial going to zero cost $70 million and led him to create his checklist.** Delta Financial was a sensibly run mortgage originator that depended on warehouse lines and securitization; when securitization froze in 2008 it violated covenants and collapsed with little equity. He is now skeptical of banks and financial institutions with small equity and large debt. _[Delta Financial]_ — [2017-12-22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z74NaYRyMJo)

### Career, entrepreneurship & life (8)

- **A small amount of capital like $5,000 is a huge advantage, not a handicap; Buffett's problem is $400 billion.** Tiny, thinly traded Japanese net-nets or obscure stocks that a fund can barely put $100K into are wide open to the small investor willing to flip through 40,000 pages. — [2017-06-07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bLjoL5zhBxA)
- **Use the 'second 40 hours' of the week for your passion, and reduce day-job intensity to just above firing level when launching a start-up.** He ran a dual life for nine months until his start-up had revenue and two or three months of visibility before resigning; his boss said 'you were just gone.' — [2017-06-07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bLjoL5zhBxA)
- **Collect mental models the way Munger does, including that people don't care that you screw up, they care that you are candid about it.** Candor about mistakes strengthens relationships and deepens trust; spend time with people better than you because the magnetic pull works both ways. _[Charlie Munger]_ — [2017-06-07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bLjoL5zhBxA)
- **Young people have lost runway, so they must compensate with a high savings rate and by building starting capital quickly.** A 26-year-old has maybe 64 years of runway; he tells students to do a net-worth analysis and study Mr. Money Mustache, who retired at 28-29 by extreme frugality. His daughter's $5,000 IRA at 18 compounding at 15% for 50 years becomes $5 million, so a low-paid internship cost her '$3-4 million', not $3-4 thousand. _[Mr. Money Mustache]_ — [2017-11-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_1aGen3q2_g)
- **Having run a business, at any scale, is a huge advantage for evaluating businesses - especially if you do it between ages 11 and 21 and especially if it fails.** Buffett's line: it's like explaining to a fish what it is to walk on land. The brain specializes in the teen window (Gates, Buffett, da Vinci all had formative experiences then); meeting payroll and negotiating a lease teach enormously, and failure makes the learning exponential. _[Warren Buffett, Bill Gates]_ — [2017-11-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_1aGen3q2_g)
- **Take a simple idea and take it seriously; successful people are built on simple ideas pursued with fanatical intensity.** He opens with Einstein's quote and says that when you study successful people, the core idea is simple and the difference is intense execution, citing the yellow bike-share company at Peking U as an example of a simple idea executed well. — [2017-12-22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z74NaYRyMJo)
- **Pabrai's own game was to turn $1 million into $1 billion in 30 years by doubling every three years, hence the 'Compound 26' license plate.** After selling part of his IT company in 1994 he had $1 million; 26% a year doubles in three years, and 10 doublings is 1024x. He compounded at over 70% a year from 1995-99 part-time, Pabrai Funds did mid-30s before fees from 1999-2007, fell almost 70% in 2007-09, and is back on track; his $1 million became $170 million despite many zeros. _[Pabrai Investment Funds]_ — [2017-12-22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z74NaYRyMJo)
- **Zero management fees are a competitive advantage, and you do not need to be full time or wealthy to run money this way; manage your own money well first to earn the right.** His fund started in his house with no staff and no expenses; his best five years (1995-2000) were part-time at 10-15 hours a week while running another company. Keep a good job for living expenses and let a small sum compound while convincing others to invest. _[Pabrai Investment Funds]_ — [2017-12-22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z74NaYRyMJo)

### Philanthropy & Dakshana (3)

- **Large inheritances are a disservice to children, so the only remaining option is to recycle wealth back to society, and giving money away well is harder than making it.** He and his wife started Dakshana about 11 years ago in his early forties, giving 2% of net worth a year to allow a decade of learning from failure; Dakshana's budget is now a little over $3 million a year, half from his family; philanthropy should swing for the fences like the Gates Foundation, the opposite of investing. _[Dakshana Foundation, Gates Foundation]_ — [2017-06-07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bLjoL5zhBxA)
- **Giving money away effectively is harder than making it, so Dakshana inverted the problem by only pursuing causes where input versus output can be precisely measured.** Unlike the for-profit world, philanthropy has no feedback loop - giving away 2% of wealth a year can continue forever regardless of results. Dakshana just finished 10 years, but the model saturates at $4-5 million a year, so gains from Rain Industries and Fiat will force them to find the next endeavor. _[Dakshana Foundation, Rain Industries, Fiat Chrysler, Sergio Marchionne]_ — [2017-11-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_1aGen3q2_g)
- **Value investing is a low calling that adds little to society, so he gives money away through Dakshana to make up for it.** Asked whether buying undervalued shares exploits others, he agrees it is 'low quality but high income' work, and says a value investor improves the planet by giving the money away, likely doing a better job than the government. _[Dakshana Foundation]_ — [2017-12-22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z74NaYRyMJo)

## 2018

2 talks, 46 ideas.

**Talks**

- 2018-10-04 · [The Ten Commandments of Investment Management](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9tGjXPhnp-s) · 25 ideas
- 2018-10-24 · [Mohnish Pabrai at Annual Morningstar India Conference on October 24, 2018](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5XJ88nRtF0I) · 21 ideas


### Cloning & learning from great investors (4)

- **Thou shall be a shameless cloner: 13F filings and sites like Dataroma reveal the highest-conviction ideas of very smart investors.** He says he would not have survived without cloning; in South Korea, Turkey and China he used cloning for cover ('I know a guy' in Istanbul), whereas in India he did direct work, visiting 180+ listed companies in two years. Buffett's 'start with the A's' was not facetious: he went through the 20,000-company Moody's manual twice in the 1950s, often buying below net cash, and in India Pabrai looks for parallels to businesses with long US or European histories. _[Dataroma, Warren Buffett, Moody's Manual]_ — [2018-10-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9tGjXPhnp-s)
- **Thou shalt not skim off the top: use the Buffett partnership fee structure of zero management fee, a 6% hurdle and a quarter of profits above it with a high watermark.** Performance-only fees stop managers from becoming asset-gathering machines, encourage concentration and cut frivolous expenses; a fund operation, like a steel mill or airline, deserves no guaranteed income if it does not perform. _[Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger]_ — [2018-10-24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5XJ88nRtF0I)
- **Thou shalt not have an investing team: Buffett manages over $200 billion of investments with no analysts, so a fund needs only about half a human to find three or four stocks a year.** He routinely sees funds with under 100-200 crores and several people hovering around; not collecting fees on assets automatically makes you careful about spending. _[Warren Buffett, Berkshire Hathaway]_ — [2018-10-24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5XJ88nRtF0I)
- **Thou shalt be a shameless cloner is the tenth and favorite commandment.** He gives his email so listeners can send him P/E-of-1 ideas, and cloned Buffett's charity-lunch auction for Dakshana. — [2018-10-24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5XJ88nRtF0I)

### Circle of competence & checklists (3)

- **Thou shall not have an investment team: investing is an individual pursuit, not a team sport, because any two people have different circles of competence.** An analyst's ideas would get rejected simply because the manager's circle differs; you only need two to four ideas a year, and analysis is the fun part you should never delegate. — [2018-10-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9tGjXPhnp-s)
- **Do not bet on turnarounds; the recovery must already be structurally in place and merely missed by the market, not dependent on management magic.** Fiat Chrysler worked because structural changes in the auto industry made recovery near-certain. In Turkey, imports have repriced but local prices have not, so exporters are the obvious beneficiaries. _[Fiat Chrysler, Turkey]_ — [2018-10-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9tGjXPhnp-s)
- **Circle of competence is the first filter, before price; but an extreme P/E of 1 can shrink what you need to understand to a single handicappable statement.** With IPSCO he only had to judge the resilience of two years of cash flows, not the moat. In Turkey a sliver of assets exceeded market cap so he needed no view on everything else. When few things survive the filters, Munger's answer is: why should it be easy to get rich? _[IPSCO, Turkey, Charlie Munger]_ — [2018-10-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9tGjXPhnp-s)

### Valuation & margin of safety (6)

- **Thou shall look for hidden P/E of 1 stocks: businesses that are a P/E of 1 on future earnings or asset value but do not show up as such on a screen.** Fiat Chrysler at under $5/share in 2012 had guided to ~$5/share of earnings by 2018 and delivered (including Ferrari), a 7-8x return. IPSCO in 2004-05 traded at 3x earnings with a third of market cap in cash and two years of guided cash flow equal to the rest; a buyer took it out for ~4x in under two years. He has found such P/E of 1s six or seven times in 19 years running the fund. _[Fiat Chrysler, Ferrari, IPSCO, Stewart Enterprises]_ — [2018-10-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9tGjXPhnp-s)
- **Thou shall never use Excel: if you need a spreadsheet to see the value, it is an automatic pass; the math must work on the fingers of one hand.** A $1B company at 20x earnings growing 10-15% cannot deliver a 20-25% return once you discount the cash flows; even Apple at ~$1T would need $260B of owner earnings for a 26% return. At a P/E of 1-3 the math becomes trivial: money back in two or three years and you still own the business. _[Apple]_ — [2018-10-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9tGjXPhnp-s)
- **Thou shalt look for hidden P/E-of-1 stocks, where next year's earnings roughly equal today's market cap; they appear in his portfolio every two or three years.** In just over 19 years of managing money at least six or seven such stocks showed up. Auction-driven markets routinely misprice; buy when pessimistic and sell when euphoric. — [2018-10-24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5XJ88nRtF0I)
- **Thou shalt never use Excel: if you need a spreadsheet to justify an investment, it should be an automatic pass.** For Rain he needed only the fingers of one hand: a $200 million company that will earn $200 million will not stay priced at $200 million. _[Rain Industries]_ — [2018-10-24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5XJ88nRtF0I)
- **Growth and value are joined at the hip; the ideal investment is a growing pie bought without paying up.** You do well buying static assets at a huge discount but far better with a growing pie. Of about 200 Indian listed CEOs he met, Chaand Sehgal of Motherson Sumi is among the best, but it is an amazing business at a not-so-amazing price, so he has not invested. _[Motherson Sumi, Chaand Sehgal]_ — [2018-10-24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5XJ88nRtF0I)
- **Margin of safety is the free lunch: buying a dollar for 20-40 cents lowers the odds of loss and raises the upside at the same time.** Like the Miller commercial, it tastes great and is less filling; there are few free lunches in investing. — [2018-10-24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5XJ88nRtF0I)

### Portfolio concentration & selling (5)

- **Thou shall never short a stock: the maximum upside is a double and the maximum downside is bankruptcy.** With shorting you will be wrong 80% of the time on timing; Buffett and Munger say they were right on the stocks but wrong on the timing. Tesla goes in the too-hard pile, to be watched from the front row, not the arena. _[Tesla, Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger]_ — [2018-10-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9tGjXPhnp-s)
- **He runs a barbell portfolio: about 55% P/E of 1s (an all-time high), 10% cash, and the rest enduring moats where he will pay up only for a truly strong moat.** Credit rating agencies are the archetype: Moody's and S&P survived the financial crisis with modest fines, no capex, 60%+ margins, and revenue uncorrelated with cost. He owns 10% (the maximum allowed) of one of India's three rating agencies at more than a P/E of 1 and plans to hold it a long time. _[Moody's, S&P, India credit rating agencies]_ — [2018-10-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9tGjXPhnp-s)
- **Buy and hold forever is not the answer even for the ultimate moat; sell great compounders when the price no longer allows the math to work.** Berkshire's Coke went from $1B to $12B in 1988-2000 (~25%/yr) but only to ~$18B by 2018 (~2.3%/yr ex-dividends); Buffett admitted not selling was a mistake. MasterCard at ~50x trailing earnings with a 2% earnings yield cannot deliver 25%; he would let a tremendous asset run to 40-45x but would be a seller at 2018 prices. _[Coca-Cola, Berkshire Hathaway, MasterCard, Chuck Akre, Tom Russo, Guy Spier]_ — [2018-10-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9tGjXPhnp-s)
- **Mutual funds with 50-150 positions and 70-80% annual turnover are like one-night stands; most investors should just own a broad index.** Businesses take years to reach fair value. In his own concentrated funds a bet is ideally at least 10%, and the top five or six stocks are 70% or more of the pie; holding 25 stocks makes no sense for a stock picker. — [2018-10-24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5XJ88nRtF0I)
- **He holds about 10% cash on roughly $800 million, and that last 10% is very expensive capital reserved for ideas that can return north of 40% a year, a 5-6x in five years.** He will not deploy the final tranche for a mere double. _[Pabrai Investment Funds]_ — [2018-10-24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5XJ88nRtF0I)

### Moats & business quality (2)

- **Funeral homes have the lowest business-failure rate of any industry because nobody enters the business and nobody shops for the low bid.** He found Stewart Enterprises at a P/E of 2 in Value Line, which he scans weekly hunting for P/E of 1s; P/E of 2s are common and usually worth avoiding but occasionally hide a gem. _[Stewart Enterprises, Value Line]_ — [2018-10-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9tGjXPhnp-s)
- **Most moats are illusions that get filled in far faster than expected; the P/E of 1 is your only real protection.** GE, the last original Dow member, just fired its CEO. Buffett noted around 2000 that only ~400 US companies earned over $200M after tax in 224 years of capitalism; today fewer than 500 earn over $500M. Lessons: stick with small and nano caps, favor P/E of 1s, and view moats with a jaundiced eye. _[GE, Warren Buffett]_ — [2018-10-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9tGjXPhnp-s)

### Management & capital allocation (2)

- **Sergio Marchionne was among the top 20 business leaders of the last hundred years, and his team's mission-driven culture outlives him at Fiat Chrysler.** Chrysler avoided liquidation in 2009 by a 3-2 Auto Task Force vote; under Sergio it went from distant third to margins above GM and Ford. Knowing since July 2017 he was terminally ill, he ran flat out to hit the 2018 plan and published the 2022 blueprint on June 1, 2018; the stock sits at a P/E of ~2 on 2022 numbers, probably closer to 1.3-1.5 given sandbagging, with Jeep at ~2M units and no me-too products. _[Fiat Chrysler, Sergio Marchionne, Michael Manley, Jeep, GM, Ford]_ — [2018-10-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9tGjXPhnp-s)
- **Performance-only fees do not cause excessive risk-taking when the manager is the largest investor in the fund and never shorts, levers or uses derivatives.** Dumb investing would hit him twice, through his own net worth and lost future fees; every dollar investors gave him in 1999 is now about $14-15 after fees, always by protecting the downside. _[Pabrai Investment Funds]_ — [2018-10-24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5XJ88nRtF0I)

### Markets, cycles & macro (3)

- **In a crash, sell cheap stocks to buy cheaper stocks and widen the discount to intrinsic value.** In 2008-09 he built a basket of collapsed commodity names that each looked like at least a 5x; not one lost money and almost all went up 4-5x. Teck Cominco, which he sold at 5x, went on to 10x. _[Teck Cominco]_ — [2018-10-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9tGjXPhnp-s)
- **Thou shalt be singularly focused like Arjuna: ignore rates, crude, currency, IL&FS or NBFC noise and see only the eye of the fish.** Brent forecasts swung from $200 to $76 around the Khashoggi affair; none of it matters versus whether a $200 million market cap company will earn $200 million. Find businesses in your circle of competence available at a quarter or less of value. _[Rain Industries]_ — [2018-10-24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5XJ88nRtF0I)
- **Neither a short-term borrower nor a long-term lender be: India's testosterone-fueled NBFCs borrowed short and lent long for fat spreads and ran out of confidence before running out of money.** Buffett's rephrasing of Polonius in Hamlet; levered financial institutions usually go bust from a liquidity mismatch even when assets are solid. To finish first, you have to first finish. _[IL&FS, Warren Buffett]_ — [2018-10-24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5XJ88nRtF0I)

### Stock case studies (3)

- **Google is a rare business that can make its revenue whatever it wants by switching on monetization engines for products it gives away free.** The founders had no revenue model; an employee later invented AdWords, and Waze ran free for years after acquisition. He bought at a forward P/E in the teens, more than doubled in about three years, intended to hold forever, but sold when P/E of 1s showed up and he needed cash. _[Google, Waze]_ — [2018-10-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9tGjXPhnp-s)
- **A Turkish coastal cement company with a dedicated port can export competitively to the US East Coast and West Africa because ocean shipping is nearly free and the lira devaluation makes it more competitive.** Cement is normally uncompetitive beyond 100-200 miles, but Turkey has cheap limestone, coal and power. The CFO candidly said domestic numbers would be terrible and exports would rise from 8-9% to 50%, then 70% if the currency fell further. He compares it to POSCO's ship-in/ship-out model and recommends The Box and Ninety Percent of Everything. _[Turkey, POSCO, Marc Levinson]_ — [2018-10-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9tGjXPhnp-s)
- **Rain Industries was a hidden P/E of 1: bought in 2015 at 30-45 rupees with a $180-200 million market cap on $2 billion of revenue, and by 2018 it earns about 35-50 rupees a year.** It traded at 10-15x trailing earnings at a multi-year cyclical low, but market forces were likely to produce very different earnings; the bet was that 2018-19 EPS would exceed the 2015 purchase price. Rain was a tremendous investment in 2015, though he gives no tips on it now. _[Rain Industries]_ — [2018-10-24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5XJ88nRtF0I)

### Geographies: India, China, Turkey, Japan, US (3)

- **In the US he never lost money to fraud in 25 years, but India carries a much higher fraud risk, so there he must meet management and follow the cash.** For 22 of 24 years he never met managements. He recommends Howard Schilit's Financial Shenanigans; WorldCom was easy to spot by comparing cash to net income (expenses capitalized), while Satyam, which faked bank statements, is a rare exception. Fraudsters are usually playing with debt one way or another. _[MCI WorldCom, Satyam, Deloitte, Howard Schilit]_ — [2018-10-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9tGjXPhnp-s)
- **Currency is irrelevant if you are right about the business.** His first personal investment in India in 1994 went up 150x in five or six years while the rupee moved 30-40% against him. At P/E of 1 valuations, and with assets that have international value, currency does not matter. _[India]_ — [2018-10-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9tGjXPhnp-s)
- **India offers an arbitrage on understanding: management teams explain their businesses poorly, so investors willing to dig in are in the minority.** Most of the Indian market is still overheated even after corrections, but in some cases there is a large delta between a business's future and what the stock price bakes in, as with Rain in 2015. _[Rain Industries]_ — [2018-10-24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5XJ88nRtF0I)

### Psychology & temperament (6)

- **Thou shall accept being wrong at least one-third of the time, a lesson borrowed from John Templeton.** Of ten stocks in his portfolio, at least four will not behave as expected: some lose, some flatline, some do far better. Forecasting a business 5-10 years out is an inexact science demanding humility even on highest-conviction ideas. _[John Templeton]_ — [2018-10-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9tGjXPhnp-s)
- **Thou shall always have a rope to climb out of the deepest well, because both investing and life guarantee deep wells.** Pabrai Funds fell 65-70% from June 2007 to March 2009, from ~$600M to below $200M against a $636M high-water mark. Like his bankrupt father's astrologer, he fired up Excel to project 2010-2011 portfolio values well above $600M and focused on that number; he still keeps the spreadsheet. _[Pabrai Investment Funds, Steve Jobs]_ — [2018-10-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9tGjXPhnp-s)
- **Thou shall be singularly focused like Arjuna: look only at the business and ignore macro clouds you cannot predict anyway.** In Istanbul in 2018 there was enormous noise, but buying at 20% of liquidation value or a small fraction of future earnings makes the macro irrelevant; he cannot forecast even his own county, let alone an economy. _[Turkey]_ — [2018-10-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9tGjXPhnp-s)
- **If wealth is lost nothing is lost; the safety nets in the US make bouncing back almost certain, so keep losses in perspective.** His wife barely noticed a change in his demeanor during 2008-09 even as his net worth fell from over $80M to about $18M; childhood extremes with his father's bankruptcies had prepared him. Tendency is not destiny, and tools like Vipassana can help. — [2018-10-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9tGjXPhnp-s)
- **Thou shalt always have a rope to climb out of the deepest well, a lesson from his serially bankrupt, levered entrepreneur father who paid an astrologer for rosy forecasts.** From the 2007 peak to March 2009 his portfolio fell about 70%, from $600 million to under $200 million with a $675 million high watermark; he broke the Excel rule and modeled end-2010/2011 values showing $1 billion or more to get out of the well. Without leverage, turbulence is survivable. _[Pabrai Investment Funds]_ — [2018-10-24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5XJ88nRtF0I)
- **Thou shalt never short: the maximum upside is a double and the maximum downside is bankruptcy, with unlimited capital calls.** He has never shorted and expects to go to his grave without doing so; Buffett and Munger say they were right on hundreds of short candidates but wrong on timing almost every time. _[Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger]_ — [2018-10-24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5XJ88nRtF0I)

### Buffett & Munger lessons (3)

- **The biggest takeaway from the $650,000 Buffett lunch was the inner scorecard: would you rather be the world's best lover known as the worst, or the worst known as the best?** He bid only to thank Buffett for intellectual property used without IP fees; Buffett aims to make each winner feel they got a bargain, stayed all afternoon for 54 questions, and told his daughters the most important decision is whom you marry. Everything about Buffett and Munger is public domain, but the lunch calibrated what mattered most to him. _[Warren Buffett]_ — [2018-10-24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5XJ88nRtF0I)
- **Ben Graham made most of his money owning GEICO, a great business, not from net-nets, and would write a different book today.** Security Analysis (1934, 1940) came out when markets were drowning in net-nets after the Depression; between undervalued non-growing assets and paying a little for significant growth, you almost always do better with the latter. His unreasonable eleventh commandment is growth at a P/E of 1. _[Ben Graham, GEICO, Berkshire Hathaway]_ — [2018-10-24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5XJ88nRtF0I)
- **Reread Poor Charlie's Almanack every year and work through the 150-plus hours of Berkshire annual meeting videos at buffett.cnbc.com.** He listens for 30 minutes daily via a waterproof shower speaker, starting from 1994 and reaching 2003 so far; Bad Blood on Theranos is recommended entertainment. _[Charlie Munger, Berkshire Hathaway, Theranos]_ — [2018-10-24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5XJ88nRtF0I)

### Mistakes & lessons learned (2)

- **The Kelly formula discussion in The Dhandho Investor was a mistake because Kelly only works when you can make the same bet a thousand times.** With a 51/49 edge and only two chances to bet, outcomes are all over the place; he would delete the Kelly section in a new edition. _[Kelly formula]_ — [2018-10-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9tGjXPhnp-s)
- **Thou shalt accept being wrong at least one third of the time, per John Templeton, because forecasting a business 5-10 years out is inherently uncertain.** Being wrong does not always mean losing money; even with a 40% error rate you hit the ball out of the park, unlike brain surgery where even a 0.4% error rate fails. _[John Templeton]_ — [2018-10-24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5XJ88nRtF0I)

### Career, entrepreneurship & life (3)

- **Thou shall not skim off the top: manage money with no fixed fee, as Buffett's 0/6/25 partnership structure did, and only after compounding your own capital first.** Buffett took no fees off the top after merging his partnerships around 1962; if you compound your own small pile at 15-25% it doubles every 4-7 years and you can live off that base. Almost 100% of young managers he advises to go zero-fee ignore him, even one with $6-7M who could compound at 40-50% on his own. The 0/6/25 structure is as close to a permanent moat as a manager can have: it removes the asset-gathering incentive and investors become reluctant to pay anyone else; he lived on 'fresh air and water' from 2007 until crossing the high-water mark in 2017. _[Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger, Pabrai Investment Funds]_ — [2018-10-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9tGjXPhnp-s)
- **Neither a long-term lender nor a short-term borrower be: keep leverage out of your life, spend less than you earn, and put the difference in a compounding engine.** To finish first you must first finish. He points to Mr. Money Mustache, a software engineer who retired at 30 on a 60-70% savings rate with no debt, as the model on his Chai with Pabrai blog. _[Mr. Money Mustache, Polonius]_ — [2018-10-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9tGjXPhnp-s)
- **Run an empty calendar, like Buffett and Munger, and constantly tweak your days so the glove fits and you are energized.** The Arvind talk is the only fixed annual event on his calendar; he avoids meetings but loves company visits. Do not take the highest job offer, take the one you are most passionate about; Buffett likens deferring what you want to saving sex for old age. _[Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger]_ — [2018-10-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9tGjXPhnp-s)

### Philanthropy & Dakshana (1)

- **Auctioning lunch with himself for the Dakshana Foundation, cloned from Buffett, has run seven or eight years starting at 1 cent with no reserve.** The eBay auction is usually run in November; the lunch can be in any Indian metro or in California or New York, and has brought incredible people out of the woodwork. _[Dakshana]_ — [2018-10-24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5XJ88nRtF0I)
