- **Follow your nose down rabbit holes of curiosity; he ended up in investing because he randomly picked up a book on a flight to Chicago.** He never worked in the industry or had finance degrees; that one book led to other readings and a new career. — [2023-06-14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tYtG7ZvMSjM)
- **Make a deliberate effort to be friends with a small number of people vastly better than you, because there is a gravitational pull in both directions.** Hang out with people better than you and you get better; mediocre relationships can have negative impacts. He says less human contact generally makes him happier, except with a few people. — [2023-06-14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tYtG7ZvMSjM)
- **Venture capital provides a real service to society but is a very hard business where only top-quartile firms with brand-driven deal flow do well.** A VC investor in his fund said his results would be spectacular if he could invest in Sequoia's trash can; Sequoia, Andreessen Horowitz and Y Combinator get the pick of the litter. VCs dressing up the pig for IPO is expected, and investors should just be skeptical. _[Sequoia, Andreessen Horowitz, Y Combinator]_ — [2023-06-14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tYtG7ZvMSjM)
- **Being rational requires being in alignment, meaning honest and candid with yourself and others, and being a harsh grader of the people you let into your life.** After meeting someone for the first time he analyses how he feels and sets a high bar: unless truly exceptional, he does not increase the interaction. His father said a good life needs one good wife and one good friend; less is more. Munger's friends, including a humble Minnesota fishing buddy of modest means, were among the highest-quality people he has ever met. _[Charlie Munger]_ — [2023-06-28](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y0K1qVJdJxc)
- **To play infinite games, be a giver and surround yourself only with givers; wipe out takers and matchers from your life right away.** From Adam Grant's 'Give and Take': givers, takers and matchers (who keep score of lunches). Charlie, Warren and all of Charlie's friends are givers who teach without expecting benefit. _[Adam Grant, Charlie Munger, Warren Buffett]_ — [2023-06-28](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y0K1qVJdJxc)
- **Keep the calendar empty, as Buffett does, so there is time to think, read and explore; freedom of time is one of the biggest luxuries.** This interview was the only item on his schedule that day. With nothing scheduled he spent the last few months studying two companies, talking to many people and reading widely until a picture formed. _[Warren Buffett]_ — [2023-06-28](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y0K1qVJdJxc)
- **Bridge correlates a lot with investing, and the data points that he was suited to investing were there at Clemson long before he heard of Buffett.** In a 1985 investing class he had a 106% average and the professor said he was in the wrong major; he only pivoted 13 years after graduating, after reading the first Buffett biography, having played Bridge with Munger for years and once online with Buffett (handle T-Bone). _[Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger]_ — [2023-07-28](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HhA8WfnEw9I)
- **Entrepreneurs are not risk-takers; non-venture-backed startups succeed by doing everything possible to minimize risk, which is the 'Heads I win, tails I don't lose much' framework.** Non-venture-backed startups are 99.999% of all startups. His barber example: a barber sublets a small space one day a week in a new town 10-15 miles away, using used equipment and no payroll, so the downside is tiny while the upside is super-normal profits if the town booms. — [2023-09-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MDuPszGThmE)
- **Start a business on the side while keeping your job, calibrating your effort at work to stay just above firing level so the paycheck keeps coming.** For nine months he worked about 80 hours a week on his IT consulting startup while employed, deliberately no longer caring about great reviews. After nine months he had three clients and more cash flow than his paycheck; his bosses later admitted they had discussed firing him but concluded it wasn't bad enough, and both later invested in Pabrai Funds. — [2023-09-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MDuPszGThmE)
- **His only 'employer' throughout his career has been the minimization of risk; scroungy startups that take no capital worked, while professionally resourced ventures all failed.** First business cost $500-600 and went nowhere, the second about $2,000 and six months part-time. The third took $30,000 from his 401K at age 25 and about $70,000 of maxed-out credit cards, but was already profitable with clients when the money went in; it reached about $20 million in revenue and was sold in 2000. — [2023-09-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MDuPszGThmE)
- **Applying Buffett's approach to a million dollars from a partial business sale in 1994 turned it into about $13 million in five or six years, roughly a 70% annualized return, which pulled him toward investing and away from being a CEO.** He applied to Buffett for a job in 1999 and was told 'I work alone', so friends who had followed his stock tips since 1994 asked him to manage their money. Pabrai Investment Funds started in July 1999 as a hobby with about $1 million from eight friends plus $100,000 of his own; he now manages around $900 million. _[Pabrai Investment Funds, Warren Buffett]_ — [2023-09-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MDuPszGThmE)
- **He started Pabrai Investment Funds in 1999 as 'plan B' after Buffett turned down his letter asking to work for him for free.** With a liquid net worth north of $10 million he wrote Buffett in early 1999; Buffett replied within a week that he works alone and 'I am not the answer'. Eight or nine YPO friends gave him $100,000 each; after being up ~70% in the first year and reaching $2.5 million in 2000 he decided to treat it as a real business. _[Warren Buffett, Pabrai Investment Funds, TransTech]_ — [2023-09-29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kfgbTNWLMJE)
- **Learning accelerates when you play with people far better than you; a great teacher or coach matters.** At 23 he was 'made minced meat of' by a frail 90-year-old couple at a bridge club, which forced him back to square one; he now plays with exceptional teachers as well as peers. — [2023-09-29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kfgbTNWLMJE)
- **His father's businesses failed repeatedly not because the ideas were wrong but because they ran on a thin layer of equity and maximum bank leverage, so the first headwind sent them back to zero.** His father was exceptional at spotting offering gaps with a very high hit rate, but was an eternal optimist in a hurry; with no VC or equity ecosystem in India, levered businesses 'were not built to withstand even the lightest winds.' The astrologer his father paid was 'the rope' to climb out of the well and start again. — [2023-10-10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w9oC1rPV5yQ)
- **He does not lose sleep over permanent versus non-permanent capital; successful vehicles become permanent on their own and he would be happy managing only his own money.** Nick Sleep's vehicle is now permanent because it is his own money, and Buffett effectively became so at Berkshire. Pabrai manages ~$900M, mostly first-generation entrepreneur families, and is fine if that mix continues or ends. _[Pabrai Investment Funds, Nick Sleep, Berkshire Hathaway]_ — [2023-10-10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w9oC1rPV5yQ)
- **Read your own 'owner's manual': he sold TransTech because running 170 people was herding cats, while investing is the single-player math game he is wired for.** He bootstrapped TransTech at 25 with $70,000 of credit cards and $30,000 of 401k, sending 200 letters a week to Midwest CIOs and calling at 7, 21 and 45 days. Industrial psychologists in 1999 told him he needs single-player, mathematically oriented games where he controls the outcome, so he started Pabrai Funds with $1 million. _[TransTech, Pabrai Investment Funds]_ — [2023-10-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jZKOk-hlo8I)
- **Working entirely from home since moving to Austin made him more productive and happier because it returns him to being a single player.** The pandemic taught him this; he now visits the office no more than twice a year and manages Dakshana and the fund's back office remotely. The fund is 25 years old and he hopes to do it for the rest of his life. _[Dakshana, Pabrai Investment Funds]_ — [2023-10-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jZKOk-hlo8I)
- **Start your kids' compounding as early as possible - an IRA has no minimum age, so get them earning wages at 13 or 14 and put it in.** He tells YPOers their runways are half gone and the message should go to their children or to YMG members, who may live to 100-120 with a hundred-year runway. — [2023-10-17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EzMWPRx9-CY)
- **You can walk and chew gum at the same time - enjoy life and run a compounding engine - but large inheritances do more harm than good.** His hero is Chuck Feeney (The Billionaire Who Wasn't), who made billions in duty-free shops, founded General Atlantic, gave away about $9 billion mostly anonymously and died with only a few hundred thousand. Pabrai plans to 'die on June 11th, 2054' down to $100, having so far given about $30 million through Dakshana. _[Chuck Feeney, General Atlantic, Dakshana Foundation]_ — [2023-10-17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EzMWPRx9-CY)
- **The YPO eulogy exercise - write your own eulogy as if you died one day before turning 80 - forces you to stop spending time on things that wouldn't make it into the eulogy.** Done at a forum retreat in Mexico when he was 40; each person read theirs by the fire, and the second part asked why you spend time on anything that didn't make the cut. — [2023-10-17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EzMWPRx9-CY)
- **He gave his kids full control of concentrated UGMA accounts worth a few million at 18, on the theory that if values weren't transferred by 18, staggered trusts at 30 and 40 are nonsense.** He and his ex-wife maxed the annual gift each year and invested it very concentrated; at 18 both daughters simply handed the money back to him to manage and never touched it, later using it for entrepreneurship and a PhD. — [2023-10-17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EzMWPRx9-CY)
- **If you're not excited to go to work on Monday morning, don't go - hit the reset button; each of his three resets felt like the abyss but led to greater growth.** Engineer to international marketing, then leaving to start his own IT business in 1991 on $75,000 of credit card debt and his 401(k), then leaving the 170-person company ('herding cats') for zero-employee investing after his YPO forum told him 'you can own the business without running it'; the new CEO sold the company within weeks. _[Pabrai Investment Funds]_ — [2023-10-17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EzMWPRx9-CY)
- **He moved from California to Austin nearly two years ago because state income tax was over a third of his total tax bill on long-term gains, and eliminating it while improving quality of life was itself an anomaly.** His path: Clemson (computer engineering, foreign student) to a Chicago telecom job in 1986 that sponsored his green card, then a ten-year IT services business, then California in 2003, then Austin. — [2023-11-13](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IJwOjG5gwAw)
- **One of his few big regrets is not taking up golf much earlier, since Munger played two or three times a week; 'we are old too soon and wise too late'.** He took up golf after moving to Austin and urges Clemson students to start early and make the most of the place and its lifelong friendships. _[Charlie Munger]_ — [2023-11-13](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IJwOjG5gwAw)
- **Even a slightly above-average investor will end up with more wealth than can bring happiness through consumption, leaving only two uses: the gene pool or recycling it to society, and very large gifts to the gene pool do more harm than good.** He gave each daughter ~$17,000 a year via UGMA accounts, invested them concentrated into a few million by age 18, and they know nothing else is coming; they have used the money to start a business and fund higher education. — [2023-11-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0qxxVBKd8CI)
- **Work for people you like, admire and trust rather than big brands that make people envious, find your passion as early as possible, and go an inch wide and a mile deep into it.** He found investing as 'an old man of 30'; knowing your passion before graduating is a huge advantage, and going all in will 'blow the doors off'. _[Warren Buffett]_ — [2023-11-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0qxxVBKd8CI)
- **His father pushed him at 25 to quit a safe engineering job because a cog in a big wheel never sees the reward of its own creativity.** His plan at 22 was to stay forever and put 15% into a 401(k) to escape his parents' turbulence. When the international group he joined grew from 7 to ~800 people in three years, his job narrowed; he built a startup on the side and quit once it had traction. — [2023-12-01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gghOEu8u6pE)
- **Luck plays a big role in everything good that happens in life, so he does not think in terms of success but of the next problem or milestone.** Right place, right time, right people; he directs all energy to what comes next. — [2023-12-01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gghOEu8u6pE)
- **The $2,000 industrial-psychologist assessment in 1999 was among the best money he ever spent because it gave him a map of his hard-coded inner self to align his life with.** The further you are from alignment with who you are inside, the less happiness and effectiveness you have; perfectly aligned people like Buffett, Munger, Gates, Jobs and Musk can go through brick walls. After 24 years he is closer but still not fully aligned, and the payoffs of getting closer are exponential. _[Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger, Bill Gates, Steve Jobs, Elon Musk]_ — [2023-12-01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gghOEu8u6pE)
- **Deliberately audit every activity, person and place for enjoyment, then increase what you liked and push down what you did not; done for decades, life becomes blissful.** After 35+ years of bridge he returned to live tournaments (Chicago, Atlanta) and concluded he must play with partners much better than him to keep improving; he will attend the Louisville national only if he can find such a team. — [2023-12-01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gghOEu8u6pE)
- **Happiness does not correlate much with wealth beyond a base level like a roof over your head; the best things in life are free.** If people spent more time thinking about what would make them happier and took deliberate action, they would get there. — [2023-12-01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gghOEu8u6pE)

### Philanthropy & Dakshana (17)

- **Donations planned for Dakshana this year should be redirected to Turkish earthquake relief.** Friends in Turkey suggested the toll could reach 100,000; SumZero has been generous to Dakshana and he asked them and viewers to send that support to Turkey instead, saying he would redirect it anyway. _[Dakshana, SumZero]_ — [2023-02-09](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ncYdcZEnH7E)
- **Dakshana succeeded because it cloned Anand Kumar's Super 30 model, scaling from 30 kids at about $800 each to about 1,000 kids a year at about $3,000 each with a 60-80% IIT admit rate against a 1.3% base rate.** He found Super 30 in a 2006 BusinessWeek article, visited the Patna slum in 2007 and offered to fund scaling; Kumar declined but blessed the copy. One alumna from a family earning $75-80 a month went from IIT Guwahati to Goldman Sachs to a Stony Brook PhD and may start at seven figures, on under $3,000 invested. Buffett reads the Dakshana annual report and requests 20 copies for family and board members. _[Dakshana, Super 30, Warren Buffett, Goldman Sachs]_ — [2023-02-28](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UcJB1m3cXKw)
- **Dakshana spends about $3,000 per bright poor kid to get a 60-80% IIT admit rate versus 1.4% overall, leveraging 30-40x in government subsidy.** Started in 2007 when he was 42, designed as a 'tuition bill' of 2% of net worth per year to learn giving early; families earning under 6-7,000 rupees a month see kids start at 5-10 lakhs, some now earning over $500,000. The government spends about 1.25 crore per IIT student, so Dakshana redirects that subsidy from the middle class to the poor. _[Dakshana Foundation, Warren Buffett]_ — [2023-04-11](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ibsxgKdJNpA)
- **Dakshana works because a $3,000 two-year program unlocks a 25-to-1 government subsidy match and lifts families out of poverty permanently.** The IIT entrance exam has a 1.3% admit rate (1.3 million takers for 16,000 seats) versus ~5% for Harvard/Princeton; Dakshana's success rate is close to 60% for IITs and over 90% including NITs, with about 1,000 graduates a year taking ~4% of IIT seats, and kids go from under $3/day family income to $150-200K starting salaries. _[Dakshana Foundation, IIT]_ — [2023-07-28](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HhA8WfnEw9I)
- **Dakshana focuses on the inner scorecard: put your head down, do the work, and let the chips fall where they may.** After 16 years the program runs on a deep partnership with India's largest government rural magnet school system; oldest alums are 32, some funded by Y Combinator, and Dakshana expects to max out at 12-13% of IIT seats. _[Dakshana Foundation]_ — [2023-07-28](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HhA8WfnEw9I)
- **Because wealth compounds beyond what he can spend, he runs two games: a wealth-accumulation engine and a wealth-disbursement engine, aiming for a net worth near zero on June 10, 2054, the day before he expects to leave the planet.** Even at 10% a year, rule of 72 over 31 years means four or five doublings, about 32x, all of which must be given away optimally. He cites 'The Billionaire Who Wasn't' (Chuck Feeney) who lives on $5,000-6,000 a month in a rented condo as the model. — [2023-09-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MDuPszGThmE)
- **Using Munger's inversion, he only funds causes where social return on invested capital can be measured easily, which led Dakshana to IIT entrance-exam coaching for poor rural kids.** In 2005-2006 he could not find a single nonprofit that measured outcomes. IIT prep costs $5,000-6,000 for a 1.3% admit rate (2 million applicants for 13,000 seats), impossible for families earning $300-600 a year. Dakshana has seven campuses, the largest 109 acres, an unmanipulable third-party report card each year, and after 16 years is tuning the model like time spent on thermodynamics versus organic chemistry; eventually alumni will run it entirely. _[Dakshana, Gates Foundation, IIT]_ — [2023-09-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MDuPszGThmE)
- **Finding great charitable causes with high social returns is far harder than finding compounders, and Dakshana will cap out around $7-8 million a year of spending.** Dakshana currently spends about $3 million a year and lucked into the IIT ecosystem. Homelessness in LA or San Francisco is a problem he is sure he would fail at. Like Buffett going from 50% a year on $1 million to barely beating the S&P on $600 billion, Dakshana will have to lower its bar as it scales. _[Dakshana, IIT, Warren Buffett]_ — [2023-09-29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kfgbTNWLMJE)
- **He aims to live up to the Chuck Feeney standard and die with zero: down to $100 on June 10, 2054, the day before he expects to leave the planet.** Feeney gave away $8B+ anonymously, died at 92 with about $2M in a rental apartment. Pabrai runs two engines: compounding assets and Dakshana giving them away; as compounding works, the giving engine must be amped up. _[Chuck Feeney, Dakshana Foundation]_ — [2023-10-10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w9oC1rPV5yQ)
- **Giving money away effectively is far harder than making it, which is why Dakshana was started 17 years ago rather than waiting until age 70 or 80.** Dakshana takes over the education of brilliant kids from families earning under $100/month (some $2/day) from ages 16 to 18 and gets them into IITs and AIIMS, resetting the family's income to world standards. It spends ~$3M/year and has begun a ~$13M capex program over three years to expand capacity. _[Dakshana Foundation, IIT, AIIMS]_ — [2023-10-10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w9oC1rPV5yQ)
- **He runs two games: a compounding engine of about $900 million of other people's money with no management fee and a quarter over a 6% hurdle, and a giving engine with high social returns on invested capital.** He does not want money going to the Red Cross or 'stupid things'; Dakshana's returns worked out better than he expected. _[Pabrai Investment Funds, Dakshana Foundation]_ — [2023-10-17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EzMWPRx9-CY)
- **Dakshana was born in 2005-06 by shamelessly cloning Anand Kumar's Super 30 after he refused outside money and refused to scale.** Super 30 trained 30 very poor kids (household income ~$20/month) for IIT at ~$800 per student with a 90-100% success rate. Pabrai expected to fall flat for 10-15 years but got traction in weeks, largely because great leaders showed up and he left them alone. _[Dakshana Foundation, Super 30, Anand Kumar]_ — [2023-11-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0qxxVBKd8CI)
- **Dakshana's social return on invested capital is a no-brainer because the government's IIT subsidy and bank loans mean the only out-of-pocket cost is the coaching year: ~$3,000 in yields graduates earning $15,000 to over $1 million.** An unsubsidized IIT education would cost $60-70,000; students pay ~$2-4,000 a year, fully loanable at the State Bank of India branch inside every IIT, and repay within 1-4 years. Dakshana graduates ~1,000 kids a year on ~$3M, some now at Google earning over $1M, others funded by top VCs. _[Dakshana Foundation, IIT, State Bank of India, Google]_ — [2023-11-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0qxxVBKd8CI)
- **The biggest value he adds at Dakshana is saying no: every new initiative is compared against the core model and almost always rejected, and that focus is why it works.** Most NGOs fund pet projects without measuring input and output; some spend 80 cents of every dollar on fundraising. The team is more passionate about Dakshana than he is, and it has worked out 100x better than expected. _[Dakshana Foundation]_ — [2023-11-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0qxxVBKd8CI)
- **Dakshana will max out at roughly 3,000 kids and $7-8M a year, about 10-12% of the 16,000 IIT seats, and its plan B is likely to fund Akshaya Patra's midday meal model.** Akshaya Patra adds 50 cents to the government's 50 cents per meal, runs industrial kitchens serving 50 schools each, and has lifted rural literacy; Dakshana cloned its rice-steaming and kitchen techniques. He calls them the only two organizations in India that think in terms of social return on invested capital. Magnet-school experiments have not panned out. _[Akshaya Patra Foundation, Dakshana Foundation]_ — [2023-11-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0qxxVBKd8CI)
- **The GFC's real threat was to Dakshana, funded solely by his pledge of 2% of net worth above $50M, so he cut the 2009 batch from 400 kids to 50 instead of pausing.** Dakshana was spending ~$1.5M a year with hundreds of kids in IIT prep and a JV with the government of India. Officials in the Ministry of Human Resource Development advised reducing scale rather than eliminating the program because restarting would be hard; the 2010 batch was back to a normal 400. _[Dakshana Foundation, IIT]_ — [2023-12-01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gghOEu8u6pE)
- **Charity requires the opposite mindset from investing: per Buffett, you should swing for the fences and be willing to lose money, so Dakshana will put 5-10% of spending into the high-risk EMRS tribal school partnership.** New EMRS schools take 3-4 years to open plus 5-6 years before a batch reaches 10th standard, so real results could take 20-25 years. On a 1-10 scale Navodaya management is a 7 and EMRS a 4, and tribals have seen no real per capita progress in 70 years. _[Dakshana Foundation, Navodaya Vidyalaya, EMRS]_ — [2023-12-25](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A2vC2skCjCs)

### Cloning & learning from great investors (12)

- **Be a shameless cloner: using the 13F filings of investors you understand and admire cuts the 50,000-stock universe by more than 99% to 20-50 names, but you still have to do the work.** Cloning trims the data set; you must still confirm the business is in your circle of competence, that you understand it, and that there is a big delta between price and value. — [2024-01-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1xpY7-uyPqo)
- **He has no original ideas; the coal bet was cloned from David Einhorn's mid-May 13F showing CONSOL Energy as his largest position, and answering 'why is Einhorn so hot on stupid coal' led to a massive bet.** CONSOL forward-sells production at least a year ahead so 2024 cash flows are known within a band; it cancelled its dividend and directs 100% of discretionary cash to buybacks, with a $1.8 billion market cap and north of $600 million of earnings. When no one is interested in cheap names, you get paid through buybacks. He never spoke to Einhorn. _[David Einhorn, CONSOL Energy, Bill Gates]_ — [2024-02-08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mi134c5X3ps)
- **Humans have an aversion to cloning, and the small sliver of master cloners owns the world; forcing himself to copy smart things gave him a big edge.** At about 20 he read Tom Peters' story of two California gas stations where one owner randomly washed windshields for free, won business, and the competitor never copied it even while losing share. Pabrai set out to prove Peters wrong and after nearly 40 years concluded Peters was mostly right: even handed all your trade secrets, competitors won't change behavior. _[Tom Peters]_ — [2024-03-20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pu8M0SsqRtg)
- **Almost everything at Microsoft is cloned and its research labs have produced nothing, yet it is ahead; Sam Walton and Costco's Jim Sinegal were also master cloners.** Microsoft copied Lotus for Excel, WordPerfect for Word, the Mac for Windows, and now partners with OpenAI on work Google did. Sinegal, asked what he learned from Sol Price, said it was the wrong question because everything he knows came from Sol Price. _[Microsoft, Lotus, WordPerfect, Apple, OpenAI, Google, Sam Walton, Costco, Jim Sinegal, Sol Price]_ — [2024-03-20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pu8M0SsqRtg)
- **Pabrai Investment Funds was structured like the Buffett partnerships: no management fee, first 6% to investors, then one-fourth to the manager above that.** A 2-and-20 hedge fund on $1 billion takes $20 million for breathing plus $20 million on a 10% year, leaving investors with 6%; under the Buffett structure the manager takes $10 million and only when performance is earned. Started in 1999 as a hobby with $1 million from eight friends, the fund reached $600 million in 2007 after roughly mid-30s% annual returns with no down years. _[Warren Buffett, Pabrai Investment Funds]_ — [2024-04-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TyYRrfY3_zM)
- **Nick Sleep found Amazon by reading annual reports until he was blue in the face, then held it as it grew to 80% of his money, showing that once you have a great business you should leave it alone.** Amazon looked expensive on a PE basis because growth capex was expensed, but Bezos's letters showed very high returns on capital and low-risk bets like AWS (worked) and Fire (did not). When the UK regulator pressured them, Nick and Zach returned capital and Nick put one-third each into Berkshire, Amazon and Costco; even after sloppily halving Amazon at 80% it went very well. The Walton family similarly keeps nearly all their net worth in Walmart stock they do not run and sleeps fine. _[Nick Sleep, Zak Zakaria, Amazon, Berkshire Hathaway, Costco, Walmart, Walton family, Jeff Bezos]_ — [2024-04-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TyYRrfY3_zM)
- **Cloning is extremely powerful: nothing he knows he came up with himself, and the world is full of great models with no clones, like Chipotle.** Jim Sinegal said everything he knew came from Sol Price, and Costco went on to buy Price Club. Pabrai wrote about Chipotle in The Dhandho Investor in 2006-07 but never invested; Bill Ackman made the money, and even today nobody has cloned Chipotle (Baja Fresh was terrible). _[Chipotle, Costco, Jim Sinegal, Sol Price, Bill Ackman, Baja Fresh, Starbucks, McDonald's]_ — [2024-05-03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FFxUSADENrc)
- **All knowledge is cumulative: most investors could not buy Consol because coal is a four-letter word and they lacked the IPSCO framework.** His reason for buying Consol differed from Einhorn's even though he took the idea from him; everything must be viewed through Munger's lens of opportunity cost, and beauty is in the eye of the beholder. _[Consol Energy, IPSCO, David Einhorn, Charlie Munger]_ — [2024-05-03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FFxUSADENrc)
- **Picking a good investment manager is harder than picking a good investment; default to an index fund unless 'seven moons align'.** Look for Peter Kaufman's five aces: alignment of interest, track record and how it was built, ethos, character, and fishing where the fish are. Being indexed forever would not be a tragedy. _[Peter Kaufman]_ — [2024-05-03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FFxUSADENrc)
- **When visiting a market with a local investor, only look at companies they have real money in, starting with their highest-conviction position.** Turkey screened as extremely cheap in 2018; his Ben Graham-style friend Haydar took him to about 20 businesses, including a bank at a PE of 0.1 that had too much hair for him. _[Haydar]_ — [2024-07-09](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jZ4f21386Yc)
- **Parents are your number one mentors, and after that the best mentors are the eminent dead who left their writings; you don't need to meet a mentor in person.** Buffett and Munger were his mentors long before they became friends, and Poor Charlie's Almanack is better than meeting Munger; he names Bezos, Gates and Zuckerberg as top entrepreneurs and Buffett, Munger and Jim Simons as top investors. _[Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger, Benjamin Franklin, Jeff Bezos, Bill Gates, Mark Zuckerberg, Jim Simons, Renaissance Technologies]_ — [2024-09-24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Run79mbS0Gs)
- **When you encounter a simple idea, take it very seriously and clone it: Walmart innovated nothing for 25 years and Microsoft's biggest wins (Word, Excel, the browser, AI) were lifted from outside.** Sam's Club was cloned from Costco and the Walmart model from Kmart; Word came from WordPerfect and Excel from Lotus. We rise by standing on the shoulders of giants. _[Walmart, Sam Walton, Costco, Kmart, Microsoft, WordPerfect, Lotus]_ — [2024-11-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DS4lhTSZMRc)

### Circle of competence & checklists (19)

- **Go down promising rabbit holes deeply for a competitive edge, and back out fast when one stops looking promising - the 50,000-stock data set is too large to do otherwise.** Each rabbit hole takes days to months, and many aren't in your circle of competence at all; deep understanding of a few businesses is where the edge comes from. — [2024-01-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1xpY7-uyPqo)
- **His process is four questions: Is it in my circle of competence? Is it widely mispriced? Does there appear to be a very large gap between price and value? Then go down the rabbit hole and ask what it looks like in 5-10 years.** Ideas start from 13Fs of admired investors. Something at $75 worth $100 is 'too Mickey Mouse'; he wants $75 selling for something worth $300-500 or more, and in most cases the answer is no. Finding one a year is a really good year. — [2024-01-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1xpY7-uyPqo)
- **AI can speed up information gathering but can't substitute for the deep dive into a moat like Coca-Cola's or Ferrari's; investing remains part art, part science.** He spent seven months in 2023 studying only coal, went more than 200 stories underground into four mines and spent 10 days with miners and at terminals, and still doesn't know the industry that well - 'people with ADD who want it on a platter in 15 minutes, good luck'. _[Coca-Cola, Ferrari]_ — [2024-01-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1xpY7-uyPqo)
- **A deep dive takes about three months, so you get roughly 20 per five years and 100-150 in a lifetime out of 50,000 possible rabbit holes; many are dry wells, and you only need to get rich once.** If one in three that look great turns out great, 20 dives might yield three or four interesting ideas and one good one. Anomalies aren't handed to you on a platter; you must choose which rabbit holes to enter and make some of them count. — [2024-02-14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZrJA8q5Yixg)
- **Be a harsh grader: reject most companies in 60 seconds or less, give survivors 5-10 minutes, then an hour, then a day or two; most ideas should die at each stage.** Whole sections of Value Line like biotech and pharma are discarded outright. Passing on Google or Microsoft ten years ago as too rich was probably a mistake but not the end of the world because more pitches keep coming. _[Google, Microsoft]_ — [2024-02-14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZrJA8q5Yixg)
- **The moment data tells you your thesis is completely wrong, you're done; red flags can come from anywhere.** Given as the answer to when to stop digging, using the dealership thesis as the example of testing each pillar. — [2024-02-14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZrJA8q5Yixg)
- **Be an inch wide and a mile deep, starting with products and services you use and love, because any business that extracts a dollar from a discerning consumer must be spectacular.** Apple's rabbit hole no longer has much meat on the bone; read everything in sight including Value Investors Club write-ups and be the shameless cloner. _[Apple, Value Investors Club]_ — [2024-02-14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZrJA8q5Yixg)
- **Your circle of competence starts narrow, limited to products you use, and expands only slowly by osmosis; be an inch wide and a mile deep rather than an inch deep and a mile wide.** There is no prescribed way to enlarge the circle; it grows as you learn how the world works and through ownership experience. — [2024-03-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yHIz0WlMnMc)
- **When something doesn't make sense to you, stop, take notes and go down the rabbit hole, because investing is the business of drilling down on anomalies, as Seinfeld does with a yellow pad for comedy.** He hated the auto industry (unionized, high capex, consumer taste) but seeing Ted Weschler and David Einhorn in General Motors made no sense to him, so he investigated and it led to the Fiat Chrysler home run. Seinfeld's book 'Is This Anything?' describes noting every human anomaly; most don't pan out, some do. _[Ted Weschler, David Einhorn, General Motors, Fiat Chrysler, Jerry Seinfeld]_ — [2024-03-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yHIz0WlMnMc)
- **Investing has no called strikes, so Munger saying no to Turkey doesn't matter; what matters is never saying yes to something that doesn't work out.** Munger was instantly negative every time Turkey came up because of the work and trips it would require, but when Pabrai asked how he would lose money on a Turkish Coke bottler, Munger said 'it is going to work.' You can let a thousand good pitches go by. _[Turkish Coke bottler, Charlie Munger]_ — [2024-03-20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pu8M0SsqRtg)
- **Bitcoin is outside his circle of competence and, if forced to guess, he thinks it will end badly because it has no intrinsic value; most people should take a pass.** The dollar at least has the full faith and credit of the US government backed by the American people; most Bitcoin holders cannot say what it should be worth or why. Tesla likewise goes in the too-hard pile even though he calls Elon Musk an exceptional capital allocator and hirer. _[Bitcoin, Tesla, Elon Musk]_ — [2024-04-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TyYRrfY3_zM)
- **Buffett's great hits come only about once every five years because circle of competence grows very slowly; the See's Candies purchase in 1972 made the Coke investment in 1988 possible.** Of maybe 300-600 decisions in 58 years only about 12 (2-3%) created Berkshire. Without See's there would be no Coke and probably no Apple, since all were bets on brands. For the rest of us it may be one great idea every 25 years. _[See's Candies, Coca-Cola, Apple, Berkshire Hathaway, Warren Buffett]_ — [2024-05-03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FFxUSADENrc)
- **Access to management is often a negative; insiders are salespeople who lead you astray, so individual investors without access actually have an advantage.** Buffett and Munger never contacted Coke management; they read about 70 years of annual reports and noticed unit volumes never fell, not in the Depression, the World Wars, Korea or 1970s stagflation. Pabrai says he has been led astray by many managers and it is better not to talk to them. _[Coca-Cola, Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger]_ — [2024-05-03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FFxUSADENrc)
- **Crypto is outside his circle of competence and, echoing Munger, 'rat poison'; a blow-up would not surprise him.** Blockchain has positives but the crypto world attracts certain kinds of characters; it is an easy pass. Similarly, AI can help narrow the universe but he is skeptical it can replicate a Buffett or Munger template. _[Charlie Munger, Suno.ai]_ — [2024-05-03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FFxUSADENrc)
- **Learn from mistakes but not too much, since a 40-50% error rate is par for the course; the richer data set is the mistakes of the greats, converted into checklist questions.** For each Berkshire mistake he asked what was obvious at the time yet missed: Dexter Shoe became 'can this business be decimated by low-cost foreign manufacturers?' and US Air became 'is it unionized, is it a low-cost operator?' This mirrors how the FAA built aviation checklists after crashes. _[Dexter Shoe, US Air, Berkshire Hathaway, Southwest Airlines, Charlie Munger]_ — [2024-06-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yjXKhLO_7jI)
- **If you don't fully understand something, such as quant investing, take a pass; that is the case with 99% of things in the world and someone else can make the money.** Renaissance and Jim Simons are an extreme outlier that almost nobody has replicated; he doesn't waste brain cells on it. _[Renaissance Technologies, Jim Simons, D.E. Shaw]_ — [2024-07-09](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jZ4f21386Yc)
- **The first step to successful investing is to buy only what you understand, ideally companies whose products you use, and never because someone told you to.** He praises the kids for owning Disney, Google, Microsoft, Facebook, NVIDIA, Nintendo and Roblox because they use those products; Kevin ties it to social proof from Poor Charlie's Almanack. _[Disney, Google, Microsoft, Facebook, NVIDIA, Nintendo, Roblox]_ — [2024-09-24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Run79mbS0Gs)
- **Running businesses through the win-lose lens lets you say no very quickly to a lot of companies without spending much time on them.** The notion appears simple but is complicated; cigarette companies and casinos are obviously win-lose, but models like TransDigm appear great and are not easy to figure out. _[TransDigm]_ — [2024-10-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m-chs2cmWTs)
- **AI and large language models are outside his circle of competence: embryonic, with many implications not yet understood and many negative.** He says the Microsoft audience is better placed to answer; so far it has not changed how he spends his time. — [2024-11-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DS4lhTSZMRc)

### Valuation & margin of safety (16)

- **Auction-driven markets serve up whatever screening criteria you set - 1x earnings, 0.5x earnings, stable earners under 3x - because things can be severely underpriced as well as severely overpriced.** Among 50,000 stocks you don't need many; one wide mispricing a year is a great year. — [2024-01-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1xpY7-uyPqo)
- **Microsoft in 2000 shows that even an exceptional business can be egregiously overvalued: at a $600 billion market cap and 70-80x trailing earnings, the stock returned zero from 2000 to about 2013 with a 70%-plus drawdown.** Early Microsoft employees who invested with him had 90% of their net worth in the stock and told him 'the stock only goes up'; the company grew enormously in that period yet holders suffered for 13 years. _[Microsoft]_ — [2024-01-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1xpY7-uyPqo)
- **Metallurgical coal was an extreme mispricing: stocks at two times earnings doing massive buybacks, and buybacks at two to four times earnings are good for your health and wealth.** Met coal is needed for iron and steel with no substitute 50-60 years out; ESG mandates force endowments out, creating irrational mispricing. His last 13F showed only coal among US positions. _[coal industry, CONSOL Energy]_ — [2024-02-08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mi134c5X3ps)
- **He invests only when he sees an anomaly, a big price-to-value delta with a reason he can understand: 'I am Mohnish anomaly Pabrai.'** Almaty was priced absurdly because of worries about Turkey and who wants a Kazakh airport; metallurgical coal, large car dealerships and Turkey are similar anomalies of price versus worth. _[TAV Airports, coal industry, car dealerships, Turkey]_ — [2024-02-08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mi134c5X3ps)
- **Once you do the work, intrinsic value becomes obvious; many aha moments will turn out to be fake, but if you set criteria and keep digging you will occasionally see something the other seven billion people cannot.** Warren and Charlie could see the gap between price and value at Coke quickly, but only because of prior experience with See's, buybacks and capital allocation. Seeing a multi-decade runway in 1988 has held up for 36 years. _[Coca-Cola, See's Candies]_ — [2024-03-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yHIz0WlMnMc)
- **He still keeps an intrinsic-value spreadsheet of his holdings as a beacon, updating it periodically since there are only one or two new ideas a year.** It was a rope out of the well during the financial crisis; now it helps educate investors in a concentrated Turkish position that redeeming means selling at market value, not intrinsic value. _[Reysas]_ — [2024-04-01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kTXZO5N_FK4)
- **Heads I win, tails I do not lose much: look for bets where the odds are heavily in your favor, and auction-driven public markets keep serving up such anomalies in hated and unloved areas.** IPSCO in 2003-04 traded at $45 with $15 a share of cash, no debt and contracted earnings of $15 a share for each of the next two years, so the plant came free; Pabrai put 10% of assets in, and a Swedish company bought it at $160. In 2023 he spent seven or eight months on coal, where a business that would produce about $1 billion a year of cash for 50 years could be bought for under $2 billion. The 'Trouble is opportunity' sign in his office is a John Templeton quote copied from Prem Watsa's desk: be greedy when the world is fearful, and when the world runs away from coal, run toward it; endowments barred from coal are why it gets mispriced. _[IPSCO, coal industry, Patels, John Templeton, Prem Watsa]_ — [2024-04-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TyYRrfY3_zM)
- **There are two intrinsic values: the standard discounted-cash-flow value and an 'owner intrinsic value' that looks much further out and includes intangibles like control.** In 1990 Berkshire traded at ~$4,000 a share (~$6 billion market cap) and a 2x-book shorthand gave maybe $6,000-8,000, but discounting the actual 1990-2024 cash flows gives far more than $10,000-20,000. Berkshire the company issued shares for Dexter and Burlington Northern and buys back below 1.2x tangible book, yet Buffett the individual has never bought or sold a share in almost 60 years; Warren the individual grasped Berkshire's value better than Berkshire the company did. _[Berkshire Hathaway, Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger, Dexter Shoe, Burlington Northern, See's Candies]_ — [2024-05-03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FFxUSADENrc)
- **'Heads I win, tails I don't lose much' is the cornerstone of investing; focus on eliminating the downside and the upside takes care of itself.** Buffett as a child walked with knees bent so he would never fall; he still calls Dexter Shoe a $10-15 billion mistake because 2% of Berkshire's shares went to zero. _[Warren Buffett, Dexter Shoe]_ — [2024-05-03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FFxUSADENrc)
- **An investor's job is to look for anomalies, things that make no sense; whatever criterion you set, Mr. Market will serve up companies that fit it.** Coke traded at 40-50x in 1999-2000 and about 7x in the 1970s-early 80s; any random stock's 52-week range is like 75 to 150 though the business cannot change that much in a year, because auction-driven markets deviate from fundamentals. Whether you want trailing PE of 1, 0.1 or one-third of book, among 50,000 global equities you will find them. _[Coca-Cola]_ — [2024-06-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yjXKhLO_7jI)
- **Value and growth are joined at the hip; every business is worth its discounted future cash flows, and the bias should be toward great growing businesses with high returns on equity even at a higher multiple.** The controversy is only what the cash flows are and how certain you are; even Nvidia's insiders cannot say what revenue looks like in 5-10 years. Paying more for growth can beat a very low PE on something flat or declining, but remain agnostic and look at the landscape. _[Nvidia]_ — [2024-06-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yjXKhLO_7jI)
- **An investment must be a complete no-brainer: if you need a spreadsheet or Excel, it is a pass; you should be able to do the math in your head that you get your money back in 3-4 years.** The investor is a salmon fisherman standing by a stream with a spear, patiently waiting for an unpredictably timed juicy salmon. The first question is what it costs to buy the whole business, the second is how long until that money comes back; more than 7-10 years and you've lost him. For example, if Nvidia at 3 trillion market cap produced 2 trillion of cash in 10 years, it is an easy pass. _[Nvidia]_ — [2024-07-09](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jZ4f21386Yc)
- **Whenever someone pitches an IPO or investment, ask only two questions: what is the market cap, and when do I get that money back; the market will deliver whatever threshold you set, from PE of 1 to PE of 100.** If the money isn't back in three or four years he is not interested. Hardcore Dhandho businessmen who allocate capital inside their businesses can do the same outside them. — [2024-07-09](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jZ4f21386Yc)
- **Value and growth are joined at the hip; all intelligent investing is discounting future cash flows to judgment day and comparing to price, so Nvidia is value at one price and speculation at another.** Buffett bought Apple on future cash flows versus price, not as a low-growth value stock; Aesop's bird in the hand question is how likely and how soon the two birds in the bush arrive. _[Nvidia, Apple, Microsoft, Berkshire Hathaway, Warren Buffett]_ — [2024-11-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DS4lhTSZMRc)
- **Even Microsoft insiders, Satya or Bill, could not give 10 years of cash flows at 80% probability; the less confidence in future cash flows, the more speculative the investment.** His response to that uncertainty, unlike Nick Sleep's, is to take away as much uncertainty as possible by favoring situations with near-certain near-term cash flows. _[Microsoft, Nick Sleep]_ — [2024-11-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DS4lhTSZMRc)

- **A revised Dhandho Investor would emphasize the relentless hunt for hundred-baggers and great long-term compounders: find two or three in a lifetime with reasonable allocation and you're done, even with a 95% error rate.** He has no plans for a second edition, but 17 years on he would explore the wealth creation possible if one is honed in on 100-baggers. _[The Dhandho Investor]_ — [2024-01-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1xpY7-uyPqo)

- **Compounding has three variables (starting capital, rate of return, length of runway) and the rule of 72 should be taught in high school so people start the engine early.** $10,000 saved at 22 in an index at 10% doubles every seven years, six doubles by 64, so 2^6 = 64 times, or $640,000, and every later year's savings compounds the same way; that is why a janitor can leave $4 million to a college. Buffett has an 87-year runway. Pabrai's own plan was 15% of salary plus a 2% match into a 401k; let it be a boring Vanguard index and the tortoise wins. _[Warren Buffett, Vanguard]_ — [2024-04-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TyYRrfY3_zM)
- **Circle the wagons: when you own a business with great economics and prospects, hang on and do not get cute about overvaluation or switching; less activity is more profitable.** He revisits the 'circling the wagons' concept from his 2023 talk and admits it skims over intrinsic value, which remains the bedrock; every business has a finite value. — [2024-05-03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FFxUSADENrc)

- **The rule of 72 is the single most important takeaway: divide 72 by the return rate to get the years to double, and life is all about how long things take to double.** At 7% money doubles in about 10 years, at 5% in 15, at 25% in 3. - **Judge management not by what they say will happen but by what they said in the past and what actually transpired - decades of unscripted earnings-call transcripts are the best window.** Annual letters are now written by PR or IR departments, but a CEO with 10-20 years of quarterly calls has a long, less-controlled record to overlay against actual performance, building Munger's latticework of mental models. _[Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger]_ — [2024-01-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1xpY7-uyPqo)

GEICO had 2% US auto share when Berkshire took control and is now double-digit, knocking on the door of the largest player. _[Coca-Cola, Burlington Northern, GEICO, Greg Abel, David Sokol, Ajit Jain]_ — [2024-03-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yHIz0WlMnMc)
- **Judging management is straightforward: ignore what they say will happen and look only at the track record of what has happened.** Sergio Marchionne had eight years of history at Fiat, Harvard cases and a book on the Agnelli family; Fiat had cycled through five CEOs in 12 months and was losing over $1 million a day when he arrived. He copied Lee Iacocca's Chrysler playbook of replacing inherited direct reports with 30-somethings pulled from deep in the organization. _[Sergio Marchionne, Fiat Chrysler, Lee Iacocca, Chrysler, Agnelli family]_ — [2024-03-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yHIz0WlMnMc)
- **Munger improved every institution he touched, including three decades on Costco's board, so subtly that they think the ideas were their own.** At the March 10 memorial Jim Sinegal could not name anything different at Costco because of Munger, which Pabrai attributes to Munger's finesse in pushing long-term thinking and the mindset that Costco is a buying agent for the customer, not a retailer. Harvard-Westlake, UCSB, Stanford and Michigan also improved. _[Costco, Jim Sinegal, Charlie Munger]_ — [2024-03-20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pu8M0SsqRtg)
- **Doing business win-win rather than transactionally, and making sure the counterparty feels they got the better end, cements trust for a lifetime and creates tailwinds.** In the 1960s Munger and Rick Guerin bought a bankrupt radiator-sealant business by paying the two aunts full face value (160,000) on notes they could have bought at a discount, and Munger smoothed things over with the mistress-executor at the California Club. Two years later when Guerin offered his half for 200,000, Munger wrote him a check for 300,000. _[Charlie Munger, Rick Guerin]_ — [2024-03-20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pu8M0SsqRtg)
- **Boeing shows what happens when bean counters replace engineers and stop playing the long game.** After the McDonnell Douglas merger, management forced huge engines and a stretched fuselage onto the old 737 instead of an 8-10 year, multi-billion clean-sheet design, leading to the two MAX crashes; with only two aircraft makers, the world needs Boeing to be engineer-driven. _[Boeing, McDonnell Douglas]_ — [2024-04-01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kTXZO5N_FK4)
- **When judging a CEO, find out whether they ran a lemonade stand at 12, because if they did not they will not be that great at business at 30.** Pabrai's own teen years sitting on his father's board at 10-11, running the gold jewelry business in Dubai and shadowing sales calls at 15 gave him an edge over engineers and marketers with 20 more years of experience. He says he had finished many MBAs by age 16. — [2024-04-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TyYRrfY3_zM)
- **It is the norm that great businesses are sloppy with execution, so Zuckerberg's 180 from spendthrift to Patel at Meta made an already great business an excellent capital allocator.** Meta was a country club with spending in every area; he tightened it up and it showed in the numbers. It is very rare to find a great business that is also tight-fisted. _[Meta, Mark Zuckerberg]_ — [2024-04-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TyYRrfY3_zM)
- **The Turkish father-son team he backs requires every capital allocation to pay back in two years (36% annualized), three at most (24%), which is why they make few mistakes and earn high returns.** Neither went to business school, and Pabrai says the same payback lens applies whether the business is tech, a motel or real estate. In euphoric environments like current tech you won't get 2-4 year paybacks, but the great thing about investing is you can keep saying no. _[Turkish warehouse company (father-son team)]_ — [2024-07-09](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jZ4f21386Yc)
- **The choice between a high-ROCE niche business and a lower-ROCE growth business boils down to opportunity cost and how much capital each can absorb; keep compounding and don't be a flash in the pan.** Berkshire faces this dilemma at 800 billion market value, needing to deploy 50-60 billion at a time, so Buffett and Munger accepted running the runway at a lower rate. Put limited dollars into the high-ROE option first, but the lower-ROE one may absorb the rest. _[Berkshire Hathaway]_ — [2024-07-09](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jZ4f21386Yc)
- **Keeping Berkshire going needs a different, simpler skill set than creating it; the real challenge is size, not succession, and in the next crisis Berkshire will shine.** Tim Cook could not have created Apple but runs it well; Greg Abel is very capable and understands the culture. Humans create crises every 10-15 years and Berkshire has the liquidity to go on offense. _[Berkshire Hathaway, Greg Abel, Apple, Tim Cook]_ — [2024-10-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m-chs2cmWTs)

### Markets, cycles & macro (18)

- **Small capital is a huge advantage: as great investors grow from $5 million to $5 billion they must move up the food chain, continuously emptying the bottom for new entrants who can make $500,000 bets.** The smartest brainpower working in small nooks and crannies of the market by definition migrates to greener pastures once it succeeds, leaving those niches for the next generation. — [2024-01-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1xpY7-uyPqo)
- **All his Turkish bets assumed the macro never improves, yet Erdogan's new post-election team raising rates to the mid-40s to sledgehammer inflation is a possible tailwind he does not need.** TAV is listed in Turkey but Kazakhstan has nothing to do with Turkish monetary policy; the baby was thrown out with the bath water. If foreign institutions return, these blue-chip names are what they will want, but it works even without that. _[Turkey, TAV Airports]_ — [2024-02-08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mi134c5X3ps)
- **US office real estate is in a nuclear winter that will last a long time; stay away, and look at home builders instead.** Office vacancy near 20% is the highest in more than three decades, worse than the financial crisis; landlords hand back keys and small banks like New York Community Bancorp get stuck. Slow population growth means the space takes years to absorb. Home builders have no overhang, low housing stock and falling rates ahead; NVR went from $10 to $4,000 in 30 years through buybacks and Pulte is following, though he has not made bets there. _[New York Community Bancorp, NVR, Pulte, Resolution Trust Corporation]_ — [2024-02-08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mi134c5X3ps)
- **The US form of government is bulletproof: the economy thrives despite complete deadlock in Washington, and a half-functional government would be night and day.** He wishes for better candidates on both sides ahead of the 2024 election but says the founding fathers built a system that keeps working through the craziness. — [2024-02-08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mi134c5X3ps)
- **The US deficit is a bigger problem at higher interest rates; there will never be a default because the US owns the printing press, but it makes runaway inflation more likely and a civilization should not test its limits.** A small deficit is fine, but structural tax changes require a functional Washington; he is not an alarmist but wants grownups in DC. — [2024-02-08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mi134c5X3ps)
- **There is always a bear market somewhere; the edge today is qualitative thinking that finds an aha moment, not more data, and broadening to other geographies reveals wide price-value gaps.** The Dow was 400 in the 1930s and still 400 in 1954, breeding a generation that thought stocks were no place to make money, which set up great returns in the 1950s-60s and after 1973-74. Munger lamented nothing was buyable, yet car dealers trade at mid-single-digit multiples and Delta and the top four airlines with airport oligopolies may be worth a look. _[Delta Airlines, Charlie Munger]_ — [2024-02-14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZrJA8q5Yixg)
- **He is the wrong person to ask about AI, but from the periphery its impact looks transformational everywhere and it has probably already obsoleted the stock photography business.** Cites an app that converts an Indian-accented outsourced worker's voice into an American accent; says MIT students sitting at the front lines of the change have a far better view than he does from Austin. — [2024-03-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yHIz0WlMnMc)
- **In 1999 Pabrai did a 180 from tech to classic Ben Graham deep value, buying funeral homes at two times earnings and steel companies at three times earnings while the dot-com bubble inflated.** People counted eyeballs instead of earnings; Pets.com had multi-billion valuations with no revenue. The day the NASDAQ peaked around March 8-9, 2000 was the day Berkshire hit a multi-year low; NASDAQ fell from 5,000 to about 1,200, a 75% drop, while Pabrai was the only guy making money for his investors. _[Pets.com, Berkshire Hathaway, Ben Graham]_ — [2024-04-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TyYRrfY3_zM)
- **Public markets are more irrational than private ones because a stock's 52-week range is often 70 to 130 while the underlying business changes little, so an investor only needs to be patient and make two good investments a year.** If his house were listed on the NYSE its quote would wiggle 20-30% above and below its worth, whereas a realtor would say it is worth $2 million day after day; you cannot buy a whole IPSCO at the stock price because an intelligent seller faces an intelligent buyer. _[IPSCO]_ — [2024-04-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TyYRrfY3_zM)
- **A stock that never reaches intrinsic value is a huge positive, not a negative, because the company can buy back shares cheaply and you collect the cash flows.** He disagrees with Einhorn, who complains that over-indexing leaves companies undervalued for extended periods. He would love Consol's price to stay low for a very long time; 'Go Nvidia', let all the money go to the Fab Four. The market is ultimately a weighing machine. _[Consol Energy, David Einhorn, Nvidia]_ — [2024-05-03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FFxUSADENrc)
- **He focuses on the micro and always starts with the business; macro is beyond his 'little brain'.** He does not start with the pandemic, US-China tension or the Ukraine war and ask how to make money from them; understanding a single business is complicated enough. — [2024-05-03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FFxUSADENrc)
- **Investing is opportunistic with no strategic plan; markets today are heavily picked over, so finding one good idea a year is doing well.** Munger said he and Buffett 'would do terribly' starting today versus the 1970s when 1974-75 was 'orgasmic' for value investors; there are now more mutual funds, hedge funds and analysts (3-4 to 1) than stocks. If he finds nothing he hopes to be smart enough to sit in treasuries. _[Charlie Munger, Warren Buffett]_ — [2024-06-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yjXKhLO_7jI)
- **Macro, CPI and interest rates are at the noise level; the less clutter in your mind, the better, so focus energy on the micro of one business.** It is hard enough to figure out what one simple business will do long term; overlaying macro mostly leads you astray. Understand the business, know what it is worth, then try to buy it at a half or a third of that. — [2024-06-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yjXKhLO_7jI)

If forced to index in the US he would buy the equal-weighted S&P to strip out tech euphoria; the Nifty has been great but he can't be bullish about 10 years out. _[S&P 500, Nifty 50]_ — [2024-07-09](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jZ4f21386Yc)
- **Who becomes US president is irrelevant to investing because the founders' separation of powers means the country works on a status-quo basis.** The US went from 4% of global wealth at founding to about 30% (200 of 550 trillion) despite frequent logjams between president and Congress. He recommends Robert Caro's books, starting with The Power Broker, and the documentary Turn Every Page. _[Robert Caro]_ — [2024-07-09](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jZ4f21386Yc)
- **As a stock picker he does not care where the S&P or the Magnificent Seven trade; among 50,000 stocks there are always exceptional opportunities, especially in a barbell market where much has been left behind.** Someone willing to dig will find opportunities even in the frothiest markets; he does not find many things but finds enough to stay invested. _[S&P 500, Magnificent Seven]_ — [2024-10-29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sDQD2CQ8MXk)
