### Stock case studies (21)

- **Fiat Chrysler in 2012 was a tough business run by a once-in-a-generation manager the market didn't appreciate, trading at a $5-6 billion market cap on $130-140 billion of sales.** Sergio Marchionne joined in 2004 as the fifth CEO in two years with Fiat bleeding millions of euros a day, giving eight years of transcripts to study. He spent four months digging (an Agnelli family book, Harvard cases); Jeep alone or RAM alone could produce $5-6 billion a year, so shedding non-performers would leave a company earning about $10 billion. _[Fiat Chrysler, Sergio Marchionne, Jeep, RAM, Agnelli family]_ — [2024-01-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1xpY7-uyPqo)
- **Stellantis at three times forward earnings goes in the too-hard pile: if you have to compete with Elon Musk - and 'Elon squared', Wang Chuanfu of BYD - take your ball and leave the arena.** Carlos Tavares is a gifted cost-squeezer ($200 suits, $3 sandwiches), but the EV transition costs legacy makers tens of billions in capex, and if Tesla and BYD earn 10% margins on EVs, Stellantis, Ford and GM lose money because the cost gap exceeds 10%; in an all-EV world 15-20 years out a negative-margin business has no value. _[Stellantis, Carlos Tavares, Elon Musk, Tesla, BYD, Wang Chuanfu, Ford, GM]_ — [2024-01-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1xpY7-uyPqo)
- **TAV Airports got the deal of the century buying Almaty Airport outright during COVID when passenger traffic was zero, owning it forever rather than under a 25-50 year BOT concession.** TAV paid about $400 million including capex, two-thirds financed at about 4% 30-year fixed. The whole company had a $600-800 million market cap while Almaty alone could sell for $3-5 billion in a few years, plus 15 other airports; the market cap is now approaching $2 billion and he is long and strong with no plans to lighten up. _[TAV Airports, Almaty Airport, Kazakhstan]_ — [2024-02-08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mi134c5X3ps)
- **Publicly traded car dealerships at mid-single-digit multiples are a current rabbit hole because the market's EV thesis (no parts and service, direct sales) looks wrong to him.** Dealers make only 4-5% of profits on new cars but ~40% on parts and service; EVs have four or five battery modules costing ~$7,000 each to replace after ~10 years and $20-25k for a full pack at 13-14 years, plus brakes and tires, and OEMs going direct may cost more than the 3-4% dealer margin. _[auto dealerships]_ — [2024-02-14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZrJA8q5Yixg)
- **Metallurgical coal will be mined for at least five to seven more decades because there is no practical alternative for making steel; new blast furnaces commissioned in the 2030s have 50-year lives.** He spent about seven months in the coal rabbit hole and 11 days in four large US mines, going 2,000 feet underground; he steers students toward met coal over thermal and says his latest 13F holds nothing but coal. _[Consol Energy]_ — [2024-02-14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZrJA8q5Yixg)
- **IPSCO (2003-04) was the template: $15 cash per share, $15 a share of contracted cash flow for two years, stock at $40, so he took a 10% position just to see how Mr. Market priced $45 of cash in 24 months.** A year later it guided another $15, the stock reached $80-90, and at 14-15 months a Swedish company bid $160; he sold at 152 within seconds. At 2-3x earnings ex-cash, management should have bought back every share, but managers are a brick wall on buybacks. _[IPSCO]_ — [2024-02-14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZrJA8q5Yixg)
- **Consol Energy is a coupon-clipping IPSCO bet: it forward-sells production at locked prices (half of 2024, half of 2025, ~40% of 2026 sold in 2023), coal is a four-letter word no endowment will touch, and it was already buying back stock.** The aha came from a Twitter post in May 2023 comparing David Einhorn's Consol bet to IPSCO; Consol was Einhorn's largest 13F position aside from Green Brick. Pabrai urged them to drop the dividend for all buybacks, which they announced the next quarter; investing is opportunistic with no strategy, you go where your nose takes you. _[Consol Energy, David Einhorn, Green Brick Partners, IPSCO]_ — [2024-02-14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZrJA8q5Yixg)
- **Buffett and Munger were rightly negative on railroads for decades and were late to the party, but once they understood that double-stacking, labor efficiency and fuel prices had changed the economics, they had an edge no one else had and bought Burlington Northern.** Railroads are regulated, capital-intensive common carriers forced to haul toxic chemicals at published prices. It took them several years to see the change; they bought the stock first and the whole company in late 2009. _[Burlington Northern, Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger]_ — [2024-03-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yHIz0WlMnMc)
- **Fiat Chrysler was a simple sum of bulletproof franchises: with a $5 billion market cap, Ram alone and Jeep alone would each produce more than $5 billion a year in cash flow, giving a valuation more than 10 times the stock price.** Marchionne published five-year guidance for 2017-18 that implied a P/E below one, and nobody believed him even in black and white. Ram, Jeep and minivans were oligopoly franchises; the rest, including 80% of Ferrari, Maserati and Alfa Romeo, could be tossed in for free. _[Fiat Chrysler, Ram, Jeep, Ferrari, Sergio Marchionne]_ — [2024-03-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yHIz0WlMnMc)
- **Reysas in Turkey traded at 2% of liquidation value in 2019; Pabrai bought a third of the company for $8 million and treats it the way the Waltons treat Walmart, ignoring the stock price as long as the father and son keep running it well.** Turkey's largest warehouse operator had 12 million square feet at $70-80 a square foot, about $1 billion of property against $200 million of debt, and a $16 million market cap; warehouses are 99% leased, inflation indexed, to Amazon, Ikea, Carrefour, Mercedes and Toyota. Four years later market cap is about $500 million, up nearly 30x in dollars despite the lira going from 5 to 33 per dollar, and the business may be worth $1.5-2 billion. The key to moving the needle is inactivity. _[Reysas, Turkey, Walmart, Haydar Acun]_ — [2024-04-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TyYRrfY3_zM)
- **IPSCO in 2004 was the classic downside-protected bet: $45 stock with $15 cash and contracted earnings of $15 a share for two years, so the plant and inventory came free.** He had no idea of long-term intrinsic value; he just wanted to own it two years and see what Mr. Market did. It doubled in 15 months, then a Swedish company bid $160 and he sold in five seconds. _[IPSCO]_ — [2024-05-03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FFxUSADENrc)
- **Consol Energy in 2023 was 'another IPSCO': a market cap under $2 billion with about $600 million of next-year cash flow already locked in by forward coal sales, a 150-year record of never losing money, and all cash going to buybacks.** The idea came from a tweet comparing David Einhorn's Consol bet to his IPSCO bet. Consol is the lowest-cost producer of some of the highest-quality thermal coal, so unlike IPSCO it is unlikely to have a losing year; the Baltimore bridge collapse has hurt shipping for a couple of months. It led him on to metallurgical coal. _[Consol Energy, IPSCO, David Einhorn]_ — [2024-05-03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FFxUSADENrc)
- **IPSCO (2003-04) was the ideal bet: $15 a share in cash plus contractually firm $15 a year of cash flow for two years against a $40 stock, so plant and inventory came free.** Pipeline purchase orders gave extreme clarity, unlike Apple or Microsoft guidance; his whole analysis was wanting to see how Mr. Market priced it with $45 on the balance sheet in two years. It hit $60 after another $15 guidance, then a Swedish company bid $160 and he sold 'in one femtosecond'; per Mark Twain, fiction makes sense but reality never does. _[IPSCO]_ — [2024-06-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yjXKhLO_7jI)
- **CONSOL Energy is 'IPSCO is back' with a big extra positive: contracted forward sales a year or more out combined with furious share buybacks.** Most of the next 12 months of sales are already contracted, with some visibility two to three years out, and all the cash goes to buybacks. Very few management teams are enlightened enough to buy back; one CEO complained the cash 'just goes into the ether'. _[CONSOL Energy, IPSCO]_ — [2024-06-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yjXKhLO_7jI)
- **TAV Airports has euro revenues and lira costs, so its costs decline in the inflationary environment, and its outright purchase of Almaty airport during COVID was a rare bargain.** Most private airports are build-operate-transfer concessions, but Almaty was bought outright for $400 million at zero passenger traffic, plus ~$200 million of CapEx for a new terminal; on a bad day it would fetch $3-6 billion. Two Harvard Business School cases cover TAV. _[TAV Airports, Almaty Airport]_ — [2024-06-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yjXKhLO_7jI)
- **His Turkish warehouse stake cost $8 million for one-third of 12 million square feet of prime real estate now approaching $2 billion in liquidation value.** Tenants are Amazon, Ikea, Carrefour, Toyota and Mercedes on long, inflation-indexed leases; 'I could not find a way that it was going to go away suddenly.' _[Reysas, Amazon, Ikea, Carrefour, Toyota, Mercedes]_ — [2024-06-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yjXKhLO_7jI)
- **His Turkish warehouse investment: 16 million market cap against 800 million liquidation value in 2019, bought at up to the 10% daily limit, now worth about a billion dollars.** For 8 million he got one-third of the company; the father-son team holds 42%. The lira went from 5 to 33 per dollar but the collapse meant nothing because warehouses are steel, concrete and land, all inflation-indexed; liquidation value is now 2-3 billion. He tells the 39-year-old son that if he is still excited at 70 they will be the wealthiest family in Turkey, just by math. The position is about 350 million and he treats it as the Pabrai family business, where he is a silent cheerleader and does no work. _[Turkish warehouse company (father-son team)]_ — [2024-07-09](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jZ4f21386Yc)
- **US metallurgical coal companies were priced at under 2 billion for roughly a billion a year of cash flow over 50 years, buying back shares with no long-term holders, so he loaded up.** Their major market is India, which needs met coal for steel but has little of it; only six or seven places in the world produce that quality, and no one will invest in or finance a coal mine. He doesn't need all his bets to work; even 40% working is fine. — [2024-07-09](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jZ4f21386Yc)
- **Blackstone is a wonderful business because sovereign wealth funds have few 'tall bridges' able to deploy capital at scale, and its leverage is mostly non-recourse.** Blackstone, Apollo and Brookfield serve funds like ADIA, Qatar and Singapore; leverage is always a negative but they are prudent with it. He judges it a win-win serving a demographic that needs the product. _[Blackstone, Stephen Schwarzman, Apollo, Brookfield]_ — [2024-10-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m-chs2cmWTs)
- **IPSCO in 2004 was $40 a share with $15 cash and $15 a share of contracted cash flow in each of the next two years, so $45 of cash versus a $40 price made intrinsic value unlikely to be below the price.** He put 10% of the fund in it despite year-three cash flow possibly going to zero; a year later it guided another $15 and the stock hit $90, then a Swedish steel company bid $160, roughly 4x in 15-16 months. _[IPSCO]_ — [2024-11-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DS4lhTSZMRc)
- **Reysas, Turkey's largest warehouse operator, traded at $16M market cap against $600M+ liquidation value (2.5% of value) with 10-year inflation-indexed leases, so he bought a third of it for $8M.** Five and a half years later it crossed $1B market cap and liquidation value is north of $2B; the lira lost ~80% but steel, concrete and land are inflation-indexed. Management increased value 2.5x in five years and he treats it as a passive family-business stake that could be worth $5-10B in 5-10 years. _[Reysas, Amazon, Carrefour, Ikea, Toyota, Mercedes]_ — [2024-11-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DS4lhTSZMRc)

### Geographies: India, China, Turkey, Japan, US (9)

- **Turkey is now 50-60% of his portfolio, not because he added money but because Reysas went from a $16 million market cap to about 30 times that, and it is still very undervalued.** Because Turkey was so cheap he bought the very best iconic monopoly-type assets: the Coke bottler, the largest beer company, the best airport operator in the region and prime warehouses. He has held Reysas almost five years since 2019 without changes and has never seen its managers make a single mistake. _[Reysas, TAV Airports, Coca-Cola Icecek, Anadolu Efes, Turkey]_ — [2024-02-08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mi134c5X3ps)
- **India has great tailwinds and franchises but is not cheap, so he has been a net seller in India and a net buyer in the US and Turkey.** Asked about India Energy Exchange, he said valuations in India are pretty heady while the US and Turkey offer more things that make sense. _[India Energy Exchange, India]_ — [2024-02-08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mi134c5X3ps)
- **Starting top-down from politics, elections or macro is the wrong way; start with a business, and look for businesses immune to macro when a country is hated and cheap.** He went to Turkey because it was dislocated and unloved, visited 70-80 listed Turkish businesses over a few years, ignored the macro and looked for the greatest businesses. The lira went from 5 to 32 per dollar in five years and his dollar investments are still up massively. _[Turkey, Coca-Cola Icecek]_ — [2024-03-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yHIz0WlMnMc)
- **Most of China is outside his circle of competence; he should never have sold Moutai, and Alibaba and Tencent did not work for him.** He no longer holds Alibaba or Tencent and only looks at Chinese names to the extent they fall within what he can understand. _[Moutai, Alibaba, Tencent]_ — [2024-05-03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FFxUSADENrc)
- **Start with what is hated and unloved; a beaten-down market is mostly correctly beaten down, but you only need one or two babies thrown out with the bathwater.** His first Istanbul trip in 2018 came from Turkey screening super cheap despite inflation and currency collapse; he asked a Ben Graham disciple friend to show only companies he actually owned, in order. High-quality businesses like Coke bottlers and dominant beer brands with mostly non-Turkish revenue were punished merely for being listed in Istanbul. _[Coca-Cola Icecek, Anadolu Efes]_ — [2024-06-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yjXKhLO_7jI)
- **He expected the lira to keep collapsing (3 to the dollar in 2018, now approaching 33) and concluded 180-190 of ~200 listed Turkish companies were uninvestable, so he bought only businesses unaffected by or benefiting from devaluation.** Persistence through negative headlines came from being heavily up in dollar terms; the handful of companies with euro revenues or hard assets get tailwinds rather than headwinds. _[TAV Airports]_ — [2024-06-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yjXKhLO_7jI)
- **India has far more tailwinds than the US, but there is a big difference between a great business and a great investment; Indian quality stocks are priced at multiples of comparable global businesses.** Varun Beverages trades at over 100x trailing PE, about five times the effective valuation of Coke and Pepsi bottlers worldwide, and roughly 8-10 times the Istanbul-based Coke bottler that has twice its volume across 14 countries; Coca-Cola FEMSA in Mexico is at one-fifth or less of Varun's multiple. India has many great investors but only about 100 businesses with great governance and moats, so all the SIP money crowds into them, and lemming behavior perpetuates until a new cycle begins. _[Varun Beverages, Istanbul Coke bottler, Coca-Cola FEMSA, Hindustan Unilever]_ — [2024-07-09](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jZ4f21386Yc)
- **Turkey is an ideal market for a buy-and-never-sell investor because the average Turkish stock cycles its entire free float every 11 days; the stock market transfers wealth from the active to the inactive.** A Turkish blue-chip CFO told him the national game is backgammon, pure luck, and the average investor wants to buy at 10 and sell at 3 for 10%. Someone willing to hold six years has a huge advantage over someone thinking six hours ahead. — [2024-07-09](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jZ4f21386Yc)
- **He had no plan to be in Turkey; it simply screened super cheap in 2018 as the currency collapsed, and now 70% of his assets are there.** He asked a Ben Graham-style investor friend in Turkey to show him only companies the friend had his own money in, starting with the largest position. _[Reysas]_ — [2024-11-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DS4lhTSZMRc)

### Psychology & temperament (16)

- **'Why should it be easy to get rich?' - undervalued securities exist but finding them takes a singular, passionate treasure hunt; per the Upanishads, your deepest desire is your destiny.** Quoting Munger and the Upanishads verse 'as is your wish, so is your will... so is your destiny': if finding 10-, 50- or 100-baggers becomes your most intense pursuit, it will happen. _[Charlie Munger]_ — [2024-01-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1xpY7-uyPqo)
- **Munger was extremely careful in life and only wanted no-brainer bets, but at the bridge table he was a gambler who overbid and overplayed his hand.** Once Pabrai figured this out he could trap Charlie in bridge and told him so; the contrast shows Munger reserved risk-taking for games, not investments. _[Charlie Munger]_ — [2024-02-08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mi134c5X3ps)
- **Investing is a game of extreme patience combined with extreme decisiveness: long periods where nothing is interesting, then a rare aha moment where you understand something better than the world and must go all in.** Two or three big aha moments in an investing lifetime is doing well; they don't last long, and the combination of patience and decisiveness does not come naturally to most humans. Looking back over almost 30 years he can see the moments where it was obvious to step up and go big. _[Charlie Munger]_ — [2024-03-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yHIz0WlMnMc)
- **The human reciprocation tendency has no calibration engine, so a small favor generates disproportionate goodwill, which he exploits in fund marketing.** Reciprocation dates to hunter-gatherers storing meat in neighbors' bellies. Pabrai sends prospective investors a physical package with a nice Cross pen and a book; only 1-2% return it, and a decent share of the rest wire the multi-million minimum: $50 one way, a few million the other. _[Pabrai Investment Funds]_ — [2024-03-20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pu8M0SsqRtg)
- **Buffett and Munger are gamblers who only bet when the odds are in their favor and never sit at a Vegas table.** Buffett joked he wanted to be a bookie but his parents disapproved, so he went into insurance. Pabrai was banned from an off-strip Las Vegas casino after taking about 150,000 over a few months at blackjack with a non-card-counting system exploiting the casino's thinner house edge; Munger loved the story. _[Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger]_ — [2024-03-20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pu8M0SsqRtg)
- **Munger's wisdom extended to reading and navigating the full spectrum of human personalities, not just polymath knowledge.** With eight kids and many in-laws and grandkids, he applied different frameworks to different people and loved Franklin's line to keep your eyes wide open before marriage and half shut afterward. _[Charlie Munger, Ben Franklin]_ — [2024-03-20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pu8M0SsqRtg)
- **Managing other people's money has never been stressful; the only sadness is investors who came in at the peak and redeemed at the bottom.** In the financial crisis the funds fell 65-67% from the peak versus about 40% for the index, and AUM went from about $600 million to $200 million, yet most money stayed. Managing money also brought friendships and better access to companies. _[Pabrai Investment Funds]_ — [2024-04-01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kTXZO5N_FK4)
- **Choose truth over diplomacy and be direct when saying no; people appreciate candor more than excuses.** Citing Power vs Force, he says not being candid is a disservice; when he declined a dinner invitation directly the person responded graciously. — [2024-04-01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kTXZO5N_FK4)
- **He prefers bridge over poker because bridge has zero luck and is purely skill; investing similarly is dominated by probabilities.** He plays four to six hours of bridge a week, Buffett plays 10-15 hours; Buffett did terribly at a poker tournament and went back to bridge. He played small-stakes social bridge with Munger for $100-150. _[Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger]_ — [2024-04-01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kTXZO5N_FK4)
- **Be a harsh grader of people: bring the three or four exceptional ones into your inner circle, exclude the bad ones, and treat the 92 you cannot figure out the same as the useless ones.** Buffett told Pabrai at the 2007 charity lunch (won for $650,000, though he was willing to pay $2 million as a tuition bill) that in a party of 100 he could only identify 3-4 exceptional and 3-4 bad people; there is a gravitational pull toward the people you hang out with and loyalty should not keep substandard people in your life. With infinite humans there is no penalty for excluding a good one you cannot figure out, but a big drain from including a bad one. Pabrai shortcut this by making Munger's friends his friends since Munger had done the filtering. _[Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger, Guy Spier]_ — [2024-04-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TyYRrfY3_zM)
- **Seek out givers, avoid takers, and above all be a giver, because when you are a giver the universe conspires to help you.** From Adam Grant's Give and Take: takers extract, matchers keep score in their heads and end up losing, givers help selflessly. Buffett and Munger are great examples of givers; the best way to get the most is not to ask for anything. _[Adam Grant, Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger]_ — [2024-04-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TyYRrfY3_zM)
- **Patience is the number one trait of a great investor; if you love watching paint dry you will do very well.** He cites Elaine's boyfriend on Seinfeld who stares at the seat back for a whole flight, and Pascal's line that all man's miseries stem from his inability to sit quietly in a room alone. — [2024-04-04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TyYRrfY3_zM)
- **You don't overcome greed and fear; you simply are fearful when the world is greedy and greedy when it is fearful, which is how he ended up with the weirdest allocation of his 35-year career.** Managing about 1.1 billion, 75% is in three Turkish stocks and another 20% in three US coal stocks; his plan for the next 10-15 years is to do talks and no work. — [2024-07-09](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jZ4f21386Yc)
- **Money made me happy, but you don't need money to be happy; the best things in life are free, and you should spend time on what you love and cut what you don't.** Many rich people are unhappy and many poor people are happy; a bridge subscription costs $100-200 a year, about 20-50 cents an hour, for nearly infinite play. — [2024-09-24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Run79mbS0Gs)
- **Poor Charlie's Almanack, for $25, has more take-home value than four years of college; re-read the Psychology of Human Misjudgment talk every year.** The eleven talks in the back half hold thousands of years of wisdom. Our brains are a messy evolutionary mishmash with wiring defects; understanding that weirdness explains why great investors bought Valeant and is a big advantage. _[Poor Charlie's Almanack, Charlie Munger, Valeant]_ — [2024-10-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m-chs2cmWTs)
- **What keeps him going is the near-infinite study of businesses and why they work, not numbers on a spreadsheet.** Gates reluctantly met Buffett at his mother's insistence and talked for 10 hours because Buffett asked questions about IBM and Microsoft nobody had ever asked him. _[Bill Gates, Warren Buffett, IBM, Microsoft]_ — [2024-11-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DS4lhTSZMRc)

### Buffett & Munger lessons (37)

- **Munger pushed BYD on a reluctant Buffett in 2008 by calling Wang Chuanfu 'Henry Ford, Bill Gates and Thomas Edison in the same person'; Berkshire's $250 million via MidAmerican is up 20-25 fold.** Buffett had no interest in a Chinese company he'd never heard of, so he had 80%-owned MidAmerican Energy take an 8-9% stake. - **The lesson from watching Munger up close: keep your nose to the grindstone on the problem at hand and never bask in past accomplishments.** Charlie brushed off reminders of his impact on humanity and instead groaned about Berkshire's uninvested cash or focused on finding a Daily Journal CEO. - **Munger and Rick Guerin in the 1960s were shooting fish in a barrel with the water drained out, for example buying a bankrupt auto-additive company's bank debt at 30-40 cents on the dollar and pacifying a widow and the nurse-executor to close the deal.** The founder, a super salesman who demonstrated his leak-sealing additive by shooting his own engine block, died suddenly and his affair with the nurse named as executor set the two women against each other; Charlie met the nurse for lunch at the California Club to get cooperation. Pabrai heard the story at a Friday bridge lunch at the LA Country Club. _[Charlie Munger, Rick Guerin]_ — [2024-02-08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mi134c5X3ps)
- **Without Charlie Munger, Berkshire's market cap would not be even 10% of what it is; one plus one became eleven because he pushed Warren toward better businesses and better people without ever taking credit.** Munger also transformed Harvard-Westlake, UCSB, Stanford and the University of Michigan; Pabrai's last one-on-one dinner with him was exactly a month before he died, and twice Munger's advice on personal challenges worked out really well. _[Charlie Munger, Berkshire Hathaway, Warren Buffett, Harvard-Westlake School]_ — [2024-02-08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mi134c5X3ps)
- **Munger, a type-A dominant partner in every other venture, said it was a total no-brainer to be a junior partner to Warren Buffett even though it went against his natural brain.** Pabrai asked him directly how he could accept the junior role given his personality; some things are simply no-brainers and you do the right thing. _[Charlie Munger, Warren Buffett]_ — [2024-02-08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mi134c5X3ps)
- **Buffett's 12 needle-moving decisions over 58 years, out of an estimated 300-400 important ones, imply a 3-4% hit rate, and one great idea every five years may be almost a law of value investing.** Outsized returns require a differentiated view from the market; such views are either delusional (Buffett probably had one or two dozen of those) or correct, and getting to conviction takes deep, slow work. _[Warren Buffett, Berkshire Hathaway, Ajit Jain, Coca-Cola, American Express, See's Candies]_ — [2024-02-14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZrJA8q5Yixg)

Munger was still placing buy orders six days before he died at 99.9. _[Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger, Berkshire Hathaway, Coca-Cola, See's Candies, Burlington Northern, Cap Cities/ABC, Ajit Jain]_ — [2024-03-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yHIz0WlMnMc)
- **Be a giver, not a taker or a matcher, as Charlie Munger was: eliminate takers and matchers from your life and don't keep a scorecard, because the world figures out extractors.** Cites Adam Grant's 'Give and Take'. - **There has not been a mind like Munger's among humans in at least 2,000 years and there will not be another; his own answer about who stands out in his gene pool was 'no one.'** In 13-14 years of friendship every meeting was at Munger's initiative until summer 2023, when Pabrai asked for a dinner that turned out to be exactly 30 days before Munger died. The body of work left behind (Poor Charlie's Almanack, Berkshire meetings at buffett.cnbc.com, Daily Journal transcripts) is what matters. _[Charlie Munger, Ben Franklin, Poor Charlie's Almanack, Daily Journal]_ — [2024-10-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m-chs2cmWTs)
- **Buffett says he is not a market timer, but per David Einhorn he is the best one: closing the partnership in 1969, the Gen Re purchase with overvalued Berkshire stock, and now selling Apple and Bank of America.** Berkshire may see froth and be positioning to deploy $100 billion or more when a dislocation comes; Buffett does not know whether it will be next year but thinks the odds within 10 years are high. _[Warren Buffett, David Einhorn, Berkshire Hathaway, Gen Re, Apple, Bank of America]_ — [2024-10-29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sDQD2CQ8MXk)

### Mistakes & lessons learned (9)

- **Selling Ferrari is a deep regret - 'we are old too soon and wise too late' - and taught him that some assets must be held when fully priced and even when they appear overpriced.** He owned more than 1% of Ferrari via his 2012 purchase of Fiat Chrysler, when Ferrari was valued at under $2 billion; it is now more than 25 times that. He will still always try to buy assets well below what they are worth. _[Ferrari, Fiat Chrysler, Guy Spier]_ — [2024-01-30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1xpY7-uyPqo)
- **His philosophy went Munger, Graham, Munger: great businesses in the 1990s, hardcore Graham after the 1999-2000 bubble, and back to great businesses starting around 2018, five or six years late.** In March 2000 Microsoft was $600B on single-digit-billion cash flows (~70x) and flatlined until 2012, while Berkshire fell from 70,000 to 40,000 as people sold it to buy dot-coms; he bought funeral homes at 2x and steel mills at 3x earnings. He should have switched back in 2012-13 when great businesses' valuations had come into line, and would write The Dhandho Investor differently now. _[Microsoft, Berkshire Hathaway, Benjamin Graham, Charlie Munger]_ — [2024-02-14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZrJA8q5Yixg)
- **His big mistake in the Fiat Chrysler home run was selling Ferrari, which he dismissed as a $3-4 billion afterthought and which became almost a 25-bagger, roughly $400-500 million on a $20 million investment.** Ferrari was earning a quarter billion a year and he was focused on the pieces that would earn the market cap in a single year; he made 5-6x on Ferrari but it should never have been sold. He missed it despite looking carefully for years. _[Ferrari, Fiat Chrysler]_ — [2024-03-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yHIz0WlMnMc)
- **Kicking the tires by visiting plants, coal mines, terminals and warehouses has been a big improvement; being an armchair investor makes you miss a lot.** He regrets not doing more field visits earlier; the travel has a huge payoff in understanding the businesses he owns. — [2024-04-01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kTXZO5N_FK4)
- **Sidestepping the dot-com bubble was partly luck from a front-row seat via private investments, while he failed to see the 2008 crisis coming and had positions go to zero.** Quoting Munger, 'we are old too soon and wise too late'; he does not dwell on luck and focuses on the positions and opportunities actually in front of him. _[Charlie Munger]_ — [2024-04-01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kTXZO5N_FK4)
- **He ignored a Clemson professor's advice to switch from engineering to business in 1984-85 and made the switch about 15 years later than he should have.** He had a 106% average in an investing class; a Disney case study showed the stock at 6-7x earnings with real estate worth more than the market cap. He first heard of Buffett 8-9 years later. _[Disney, Warren Buffett]_ — [2024-05-03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FFxUSADENrc)
- **He was 80-90% in tech growth stocks from 1994-99, switched entirely to deep value at the top of the bubble, then stayed in deep value about six years too long.** A failed private dot-com (he lost ~$3 million, outside investors ~$2 million) gave him a three-month look-ahead at the bubble. On March 9, 2000, the day NASDAQ peaked, Berkshire hit a multi-year low as people sold it for pets.com. Buying funeral homes and oil tankers, the funds did 37% a year before fees from 1999-2007 with no down years; by 2011-12 he should have gone back to better businesses. _[Berkshire Hathaway, Pabrai Investment Funds]_ — [2024-06-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yjXKhLO_7jI)
- **Valeant blew up Sequoia, Pershing Square and ValueAct because these very smart investors missed something basic: the business model was win-lose.** In mid-2015 Ruane Cunniff had $7.5B of a $21B portfolio in Valeant, Ackman ~$4B of $14B, Ubben ~$3.3B of $20B. Valeant's ex-McKinsey CEO bought small drug companies, gutted R&D and raised prices on life-saving patented drugs as high as they could get away with, a 'chain letter' as Buffett called it. Munger called the strategy deeply immoral and said 'sewer' was too light a word while the stock was still flying high. _[Valeant, Sequoia Fund, Ruane Cunniff, Bill Ackman, Pershing Square, Jeff Ubben, ValueAct]_ — [2024-10-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m-chs2cmWTs)
- **If a stock is flat or down after three years there is a decent probability your assessment was wrong, but do a holistic analysis rather than sell automatically.** Revisiting the Dhandho Investor two-to-three-year rule: the best investors are wrong one in three times and many are wrong half the time; the stock may still be undervalued, but there may be factors affecting intrinsic value you do not understand. Investing forgives a high error rate. _[The Dhandho Investor]_ — [2024-10-29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sDQD2CQ8MXk)

Fast forward 10-20 years and that list of companies you already pay will contain 50-baggers. _[Facebook, Chipotle, Sweetgreen]_ — [2024-03-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yHIz0WlMnMc)

### Philanthropy & Dakshana (30)

- **Philanthropy has the opposite rules from investing: go high risk, high return, swing for the fences and don't care about a high probability of failure, as long as success moves the needle.** The Gates Foundation has spent decades on vaccines with little to show, but a malaria vaccine would change the game as polio and smallpox did. - **He cloned Buffett's giving formula: give a fixed percentage each year (2% of net worth from 2007, when it exceeded $50 million) so that compounding above the giving rate means the dollars given keep rising forever.** Buffett gives 5% of his remaining Berkshire shares each year to four or five foundations; because intrinsic value grows faster than 5%, he'd still be giving more each year if he lived a thousand years. Pabrai's first-year giving in 2007 was about $1.3-1.4 million. He calls himself a shameless cloner. _[Warren Buffett, Dakshana Foundation, Berkshire Hathaway]_ — [2024-03-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yHIz0WlMnMc)
- **Keep separation of church and state: never mix investing with saving the planet, because the two mindsets are different and combining them won't get you to the promised land.** When he looks at philanthropy he looks only at philanthropy, and when investing only at investing; Dakshana is focused solely on social impact, whose return on invested capital is so extreme that the next five ventures could fail and it would still be fine. _[Dakshana Foundation]_ — [2024-03-12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yHIz0WlMnMc)
- **Munger gave about half his roughly 2 billion net worth to his eight children in 2010, the one year with no US estate tax, and focused on giving the rest away.** Each child received about 125 million in Berkshire stock, now worth roughly 400 million, and they have done impressive and varied philanthropic work. He likely still had a couple of billion at death. _[Charlie Munger, Berkshire Hathaway]_ — [2024-03-20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pu8M0SsqRtg)
- **Not believing in large inheritances forces you to give money away; Dakshana was built only because the model's originator would not scale, so he cloned it.** Started in 2006-2007 with the intention of just writing checks, Dakshana blew away his most optimistic goals and enriched his life; today he would give to one or two nonprofits that do a good job if they could absorb the amounts. _[Dakshana]_ — [2024-04-01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kTXZO5N_FK4)
- **Being a giver does not require wealth; Dakshana's poor scholars give their time, and reliable, honest, high-integrity people almost never do terribly in life.** His rebuttal to skeptics of Dakshana's 'give, give, give' model is that it is hard to find examples of very reliable, hardworking, high-integrity people who failed. _[Dakshana]_ — [2024-04-01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kTXZO5N_FK4)
- **Philanthropy should be viewed through the lens of a capital allocator, because input-to-output ratios are fundamental to investing and equally decisive when resources for doing good are limited.** Feeding a hungry man outside a temple, sheltering a homeless family in Bangalore, or a needle program for addicts in Los Angeles all do good, but if you knew which had the highest return you would fund only that one. Most nonprofits never ask the question because it is too hard to answer; Nobel laureates Esther Duflo and Abhijit Banerjee are among the few who try to measure it. _[Esther Duflo, Abhijit Banerjee]_ — [2024-06-19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uzp37XkxWxY)
- **Nonprofits have no feedback loop: a foundation spending the required 5% while earning 7-8% will exist forever regardless of whether it helps anyone, whereas capitalism's creative destruction wipes out companies that stop delivering value.** A $1 billion Rockefeller or Ford Foundation spends $50 million a year and makes $70-80 million, so it grows even if the spending is useless; Infosys, by contrast, would go bankrupt if it provided poor service. Nonprofits that want to optimize must artificially impose rules that almost none know or apply. _[Rockefeller Foundation, Ford Foundation, Infosys]_ — [2024-06-19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uzp37XkxWxY)
- **Dakshana inverted the measurement problem, following Munger's 'invert, always invert': instead of picking a cause and struggling to measure it, pick causes where outcome measurement is easy, which led to education.** Education outcomes are obvious, and teaching a man to fish implicitly has a higher social return on invested capital than giving fish. Over 17 years about 70% of Dakshana scholars have been admitted to IITs, close to 90% to IITs or NITs, and around 95% to some engineering college. _[Dakshana, Charlie Munger]_ — [2024-06-19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uzp37XkxWxY)
- **Dakshana spends about 2.5 lakhs per scholar and can take a family from 60,000 rupees a year to nearly 2 crores a year within six years, a 10x-plus income transformation almost no other intervention could achieve.** Rajiv Kumar from Fatehpur district, whose parents earned under 5,000 rupees a month, graduated IIT Kanpur in 2014 and earns 1.9 crores a year at Google Bangalore, or about $800,000 if he moved to Mountain View. The social impact on his siblings, cousins and future generations approaches infinity and is not worth trying to measure. _[Dakshana, Rajiv Kumar, Google, IIT Kanpur]_ — [2024-06-19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uzp37XkxWxY)
- **The Dakshana 'hack' or jugaad is that admission to an IIT unlocks roughly 80 lakhs of government subsidy per student, so 2.5 lakhs of coaching leverages a program never intended to alleviate poverty into one that does.** Unsubsidized IIT would cost 15-20 lakhs a year, about 80 lakhs for four years, and the subsidy goes equally to Ambani's son and the poorest student, a stupid public policy. IIT coaching costs 3-5 lakhs, impossible for a family earning 60,000 rupees a year; if Dakshana had to pay the full 82.5 lakhs per kid its return would be terrible, since that sum in a bank yields 4-5 lakhs a year on its own. _[Dakshana, IIT]_ — [2024-06-19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uzp37XkxWxY)
- **The IITs were meant to take the best talent of India but in practice took the best of urban middle-class India, excluding 85-90% of the country, because rural and poor kids face awareness, coaching-availability and affordability problems.** Kids in the Sundarbans, the Andaman Islands, Arunachal Pradesh or Fatehpur have never heard the word IIT and have no high-quality coaching; excluding rural India alone excludes about 900 million people. Dakshana has sent a girl from the Andamans and kids from Kargil and the Sundarbans to IIT. _[Dakshana, IIT]_ — [2024-06-19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uzp37XkxWxY)
- **Dakshana piggybacks on the Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya system, Rajiv Gandhi's biggest and least-known achievement: 660 free residential Doon-School-style boarding schools, one per district, that admit the top 1% of fifth graders via a language-independent IQ test.** About 40 lakh kids a year take the test for 40,000 seats, all selected centrally in Delhi on 30-acre campuses following CBSE in English medium. In 2007 Pabrai received a 40,000-row spreadsheet of 10th-standard scores in Irvine, cut it to 4,000 in ten minutes, tested them at 30-40 centers and took about 400, so getting 80-90% into IIT is unsurprising because they have brains coming out of their ears. _[Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya, Rajiv Gandhi, Narasimha Rao, The Doon School, Dakshana]_ — [2024-06-19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uzp37XkxWxY)
- **Dakshana now takes about 1,000 kids a year across IIT, NIT, AIIMS and government medical colleges at roughly $2,500 per kid, spending about $2.5 million (20 crores) a year and expanding its Pune campus from 600 to 1,100 kids with a $12 million investment.** The 109-acre Pune campus expansion will take three years and push annual spending to $4-5 million. Dakshana also built the Charles T. Munger Hall in Bangalore near Yelahanka for about $3.5 million, coaching 240 kids at a time. _[Dakshana, Charles T. Munger Hall, Pune]_ — [2024-06-19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uzp37XkxWxY)
- **Digital and online education would let Dakshana reach far more kids but yields for the IIT entrance exam would drop a lot; Dakshana is an inch wide and a mile deep and must decide whether to become a mile wide and an inch deep.** He recently spoke with Physics Wallah, which offered to collaborate and provide digital resources for free; Dakshana is evaluating it. _[Physics Wallah, Dakshana]_ — [2024-06-19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uzp37XkxWxY)
- **He cloned Buffett's giving formula, starting by donating 2% of his wealth a year (about $1 million on $50 million at the time), with the goal of having exactly 5,000 rupees to his name on June 10, 2054, the day before he plans to leave Planet Earth.** He runs two engines, one compounding wealth and one giving it away, and the giving engine must step up big time: from $2.5-3 million a year to $10-20 million in a few years and $30-40 million after that. Return on invested capital will fall as scale rises, as it has for the Gates Foundation, but that is fine if absolute numbers go up. _[Warren Buffett, Dakshana, Gates Foundation]_ — [2024-06-19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uzp37XkxWxY)
- **Chuck Feeney is his hero: the Duty Free International and General Atlantic founder gave away billions mostly anonymously and died in a rented San Francisco studio with under $100,000 left.** Feeney's objective was to have nothing left when he died; even the remaining assets were given away by his family afterward. Pabrai intends to follow Chuck's example. _[Chuck Feeney, Duty Free International, General Atlantic]_ — [2024-06-19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uzp37XkxWxY)
- **He is willing to simply write checks to other high-return nonprofits rather than keep everything homegrown, but worries that organizations may be unable to absorb and scale the money.** Akshaya Patra's midday meal program in Bangalore generates a very high social return on invested capital; if he offered it $2 million a year it might say it cannot scale. He is also studying Foundation for Excellence, Teach for India and The Nudge. _[Akshaya Patra Foundation, Foundation for Excellence, Teach for India, The Nudge]_ — [2024-06-19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uzp37XkxWxY)
- **Start philanthropy early, when you still have energy to experiment and pay the tuition of failures, rather than just writing checks in your seventies.** He started Dakshana at 42 when net worth crossed $50 million, giving 2% of net worth a year (at least $1 million), fully expecting 5-15 years of failure; instead traction came within weeks and things went 10 times better than expected. He is now 60 with 18 years of experience. _[Dakshana Foundation]_ — [2024-10-29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sDQD2CQ8MXk)
- **For seven-figure annual giving a family foundation makes sense, and public charity status unlocks corporate matching from Microsoft, Google and IBM donors.** Dakshana began as a US 501(c)(3) family foundation plus an Indian charitable trust, later obtaining IRS public charity status; donating appreciated stock has tax advantages. _[Dakshana Foundation, Microsoft, Google, IBM]_ — [2024-10-29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sDQD2CQ8MXk)
- **Philanthropy lacks the two feedback loops capitalism has: an endowed foundation survives forever without being useful, and outcomes for 98% of causes are almost impossible to measure.** A foundation earning 6% and spending the IRS-required 5% keeps growing even if it makes a bonfire of the money; a free-needle program for the homeless has some benefit but nobody can measure it. Without measurement you cannot decide what to increase or decrease. _[Rockefeller Foundation]_ — [2024-10-29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sDQD2CQ8MXk)
- **Following Munger's 'invert, always invert', Dakshana only pursues activities where output per unit of input is easy to measure, which led to education for very poor, very smart kids.** Education has a huge multiplier effect, turning zeros into heroes. He contrasts Gottesman's $1 billion gift making Albert Einstein medical school tuition-free, where return on capital differs vastly between rich and needy students and may never be measured. _[Charlie Munger, Albert Einstein College of Medicine, Gottesman]_ — [2024-10-29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sDQD2CQ8MXk)
- **The IIT entrance exam is a strict, purely objective meritocracy with a 1.3% admit rate, which makes it an ideal ecosystem for measurable social return.** About 1.3 million kids compete for 16,000 seats; a 33% score gets a seat while top-96 ranks score 90%+. IIT is nearly free once admitted. Bill Gates said if limited to one school for Microsoft recruiting he would pick the IITs over MIT and Stanford. _[IIT, Bill Gates, Microsoft]_ — [2024-10-29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sDQD2CQ8MXk)
- **Dakshana's $3,000 per kid can transform a family from $50 a month to $80,000 a month, as with Ashok, a Hyderabad slum kid who ranked 63 at IIT and now earns over $1 million a year at Google.** Ashok scored 27/100 on his first IIT Bombay CS test, 'found another gear', graduated in the top 15%, and got Google Skype interviews within seven hours of emailing HR with his rank. Dakshana takes about 1,000 kids a year with a 70% IIT admit rate and 15% AIIMS admit rate versus 0.1% nationally. _[Dakshana Foundation, Google, IIT Bombay, AIIMS]_ — [2024-10-29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sDQD2CQ8MXk)
- **Vertical integration brought Dakshana's cost per kid down from about $5,000 to $3,000 despite 18 years of inflation, and its coaching now beats the for-profit industry.** It began as an outsourced model paying for-profit coaching centers; now it has its own 109-acre campus in Pune, faculty paid $60-80,000 (half a million US-equivalent), many of them alumni. Wealthy parents offer $20-30,000 a year for a seat and are refused; it is free or nothing. _[Dakshana Foundation]_ — [2024-10-29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sDQD2CQ8MXk)
- **Dakshana will hit a brick wall at about $7-8 million a year of spending because it would run out of IIT seats; it already fills 3-4% of them and can never exceed about 1 in 8.** Spending is about $3 million now with $10 million of capex under way to reach 1,500 kids a year and roughly $5 million a year in three years; rich kids start coaching in 6th grade for six years while Dakshana coaches for one year after 12th. _[Dakshana Foundation, IIT]_ — [2024-10-29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sDQD2CQ8MXk)
- **Focus and feedback loops matter in charity: push one model to its limit, accept that future models will have far lower returns, and treat setbacks as block-and-tackle problems.** The first batch had only a 10% IIT success rate because outsourced coaches sent third-rate faculty or nobody at all; he fired them ('fool me twice, shame on me') and the rate went to 20% and kept rising. Targets $10 million a year, about 5% of a hoped-for $200 million net worth; his net worth was cut in half by divorce but stayed above $50 million. _[Dakshana Foundation]_ — [2024-10-29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sDQD2CQ8MXk)
- **Well-run charter schools like Joel Greenblatt's Success Academy earn a very high return on private dollars because they are layered on top of public base funding.** Ivy League teachers meet inner-city minority students; he judges Success Academy's return higher than the Gottesman gift when viewed through the input-output lens investors already use. _[Success Academy, Joel Greenblatt]_ — [2024-10-29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sDQD2CQ8MXk)
- **In philanthropy stay very narrow and say no 99% of the time; sprinkling money across causes does not work.** Exceptions were small: $10,000 to Success Academy for lunch with Greenblatt, the Buffett lunch donation to Glide, and Turkey earthquake contributions because he has investments there and should not take without giving. _[Glide Foundation, Success Academy]_ — [2024-10-29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sDQD2CQ8MXk)
- **He is a single-player game player running two games: compound at ~25-26% (a million to a billion in 30 years) and give it all away to be left with $10,000 the day before he dies.** He started the compounding game exactly 30 years ago; beyond a point money doesn't correlate with happiness, so following Chuck Feeney and Buffett he blasts the money out through Dakshana, which he calls just a math game. _[Dakshana Foundation, Chuck Feeney, Warren Buffett]_ — [2024-11-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DS4lhTSZMRc)
