Bring in the best, make trade free and fair, and 'let it rip'. — [2025-06-10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jW-L5NdvYkU)

### Psychology & temperament (17)

- **He saw Meta as an easy double but never bought it because of a mental block about multi-trillion market caps and the law of large numbers, which he admits is sometimes wrong.** He is skeptical of where NVIDIA, Microsoft or Apple are in 10-20 years; at the time other names looked more interesting. _[Meta, NVIDIA, Microsoft, Apple]_ — [2025-01-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MGqKFwtCWnU)
- **Risk and uncertainty are different; high uncertainty combined with low risk gives great rewards to the patient, whereas seeking certainty means paying a high price for a cheery consensus.** Patience is the most important skill because businesses rarely play out as expected; coal fits the low-risk, high-uncertainty equation, and one should love watching paint dry. _[Warren Buffett]_ — [2025-01-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MGqKFwtCWnU)
- **'To encounter misfortune and overcome it is good fortune': every major setback in his life has been the kernel of later growth, so he now has blind faith that adversity will prove helpful.** Munger lost a son to leukemia and an eye to a botched cataract operation around 60 and his answer was 'you always just soldier on'. Pabrai cannot point to a single setback that did not lead to better outcomes. _[Marcus Aurelius, Charlie Munger]_ — [2025-01-31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JpGi2c7a1gw)
- **The number one investing skill is extreme patience, coupled with a thesis so simple it fits in three or four sentences a 10- or 12-year-old could follow.** Even Reysas, extraordinarily undervalued, did nothing for a couple of years. Many stocks drop 50% after you buy them; without a hardcoded, simple thesis you will second-guess and sell, but if the thesis is intact after the drop, conviction stays intact. _[Reysas]_ — [2025-01-31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JpGi2c7a1gw)
- **Measure yourself by the inner scorecard, not the outer one; it becomes the baseline for growth because you have no illusions about your flaws.** Buffett's test: would you rather be known as the best lover in the world but know you are the worst, or vice versa? Knowing the answer puts you far along toward success. _[Warren Buffett]_ — [2025-02-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HSq4QOCuuDA)
- **Following Marcus Aurelius, to encounter misfortune and overcome it is good fortune; every adversity in his life has led to greater growth, so he now smiles through challenges.** At almost 61 he says there is no case where adversity did not produce growth; confront it head-on with faith that tomorrow will be better, which means there is never a downside in life. _[Marcus Aurelius]_ — [2025-02-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HSq4QOCuuDA)
- **If wealth is lost nothing is lost; the US safety net means poor people are fat, so losing a job or a drawdown is not something to fear.** His father went bankrupt several times with heavy leverage and no savings, so the family relied on friends for groceries and rent; as an adult he put 15% of salary into his 401k from day one to never repeat that. — [2025-02-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HSq4QOCuuDA)
- **Bridge makes you a better investor because it trains probabilistic thinking: every card played changes the odds and you must recalculate.** Bridge takes 15 minutes to learn and cannot be mastered in a lifetime, like investing where you never plateau; he played bridge long before investing and found it built the probability muscle. Buffett plays serious duplicate bridge (username T Bone, partner Sharon Osberg) while Munger was a social, bluffing gambler at the table despite being regimented in investing. _[Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger, Bill Gates]_ — [2025-02-25](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Eww63NIxKew)
- **Adversity is a blessing; every difficult period in his life led to greater growth and higher highs, so when a reverse comes you should be excited and grateful even without knowing how it will help.** He draws on Marcus Aurelius's Stoicism and Munger's point that no one is immune from reverses. He now observes his own adversity almost as an outsider, confident it leads to higher highs: play the cards and life works out. _[Marcus Aurelius, Charlie Munger]_ — [2025-04-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ePBZbS0cRAM)
- **The reciprocation tendency is hardwired but uncalibrated: a $30 Cross pen in a physical mailer creates a favorable opinion that can bring in $10 million.** Hunter-gatherers stored meat in neighbors' bellies via feasts, encoding reciprocation; Pabrai Funds sends prospects a package with a book, pen and hard copies, and only one or two in a hundred return it because of the friction of doing so. _[Pabrai Investment Funds]_ — [2025-04-22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YBinkgDRPHo)
- **Ask 'What is going on here?' whenever something makes you do a double-take, a lesson from playing duplicate bridge with a former world champion.** His partner Roger, world champion at 23, plays as if opponents' cards are exposed by constantly asking that question; Pabrai applies it to anomalies in markets. — [2025-04-22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YBinkgDRPHo)
- **Less is more, and fast is slow.** Buffett was forced into five Japanese bets only because of Berkshire's size. Duan Yongping, founder of Oppo and Vivo, told his managers only 'fast is slow' in a 10-minute annual meeting and they tripled profits the next year. _[Duan Yongping, Oppo, Vivo, Warren Buffett]_ — [2025-05-02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NrTz1uiL3RU)
- **Investors must be able to sit quietly and do nothing for decades; the hack is to find another passion that soaks up all the time so the portfolio is left untouched.** Munger says it was good Buffett played bridge; Buffett says you can give away 50 IQ points and results might improve. Pabrai has gone all in on golf and says no new ideas for 5 or 10 years would be fine. Hedging a great position is 'getting cute' like Nick Sleep buying ASOS. _[Nick Sleep, Charlie Munger, Warren Buffett, ASOS]_ — [2025-05-02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NrTz1uiL3RU)
- **Be a giver, not a taker or matcher: don't play math games on favors, always let the other guy get the better end, and the goodwill compounds.** From Adam Grant's Givers and Takers: takers go nowhere and should be cut out of your life; givers become the most successful because the universe conspires to help them. The key is not doing it to get anything back. _[Adam Grant]_ — [2025-07-13](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vNBluvpgphs)
- **Day trading is not good; the brokers make all the money and there are no day traders in the Forbes 400.** Robinhood will profit, not the young men drawn in by ads. Crypto is outside his competence so he does not touch it. _[Robinhood]_ — [2025-07-13](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vNBluvpgphs)
- **Eliminating white lies and preferring truth over diplomacy builds trust, which is a real edge in life, per David Hawkins' Power vs. Force.** Hawkins argues the subconscious detects lies even when the conscious mind does not. Post-Hawkins he tells his wife when a dress doesn't work, taking short-term pain for a stronger relationship. Truth is on a log curve: Jesus, Buddha and Gandhi at the extreme, Buffett and Munger a bit below; Munger says the world runs on trust, not contracts. _[David Hawkins, Charlie Munger, Warren Buffett]_ — [2025-10-14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fW9j-mDNVt8)
- **All investment manager misery stems from the inability to sit quietly in a room alone and do nothing; activity is the single biggest issue.** He adapted Pascal's quote and says learning to enjoy watching paint dry took him a very long time and he is still trying to get better at it. _[Blaise Pascal]_ — [2025-10-14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fW9j-mDNVt8)

### Buffett & Munger lessons (15)

- **Investments do not fall into neat buckets of 'great business' versus 'special situation'; flexibility and second-order thinking matter, like Buffett's Swiss Army knife.** Berkshire, with $100 billion-plus in cash, still borrowed nearly the entire amount in yen to buy the Japanese trading companies because it was mathematically right, earning an effectively infinite return on equity; the ideal remains great businesses at great prices that return 10-100x over 10-20 years. _[Berkshire Hathaway, Japanese trading companies, Google]_ — [2025-01-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MGqKFwtCWnU)
- **Buffett has a 'Swiss Army knife' approach: mostly great businesses, but he still enjoys workouts like the Japanese trading companies financed entirely with 0.5% yen debt against 8% dividend yields.** Without putting up equity he was significantly cash-flow positive; the companies then doubled dividends, taking the yield on cost to 15%, and the stock prices doubled too. Be flexible and read a lot until something truly exceptional shows up on the radar. _[Warren Buffett, Japanese trading companies, Charlie Munger]_ — [2025-01-31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JpGi2c7a1gw)
- **Paying $650,000 for the 2007 Buffett lunch was a cheap 2-3% tuition bill on the $70M+ of net worth attributable to Buffett's teachings, and it turned into 'buy one lunch, get infinite lunches free'.** He had bid unsuccessfully since 2004; the last lunch went for $26M. The lunch led to a friendship with Charlie Munger, dinners every couple of months and being his Bridge partner at the LA Country Club. _[Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger, Guy Spier]_ — [2025-02-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HSq4QOCuuDA)
- **Buffett told his daughters, then 10 and 12, that the most important decision in life is whom you marry, which needs a balance of heart and head.** Buffett said he had nothing going on all afternoon and would stay as long as they wanted; he converts every 'lemon' question into lemonade with a lesson. _[Warren Buffett]_ — [2025-02-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HSq4QOCuuDA)
- **Munger told me 'you only need to get rich once'; trying to optimize compounding is a mistake that blew up in my face, and once you know you hold a compounder you sell only on true secular decline, never on valuation.** Not a down quarter, a wiggle or a recession, but a genuine secular decline in the business is the only worthy reason to consider selling. _[Charlie Munger]_ — [2025-02-25](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Eww63NIxKew)
- **Munger's pie counter: you get only three or four trips in a lifetime, so load up on a lot of pie and keep it; I blew trips on Ferrari and on Frontline, which I sold after a double and which became a 70x in three years.** Every few months Munger would recite the same successful trips (Berkshire, Costco, Li Lu, apartment houses) and was content if there were no more; with 30 years left Pabrai hopes for two or three more trips but says the pies already held cannot be let go. _[Charlie Munger, Ferrari, Frontline, Berkshire Hathaway, Costco, Li Lu]_ — [2025-02-25](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Eww63NIxKew)
- **Great investment ideas are rare; Buffett said 12 decisions in 58 years moved the needle at Berkshire, roughly one good idea every five years and a 4% hit rate.** From Buffett's 2022 letter; out of 300-400 purchase decisions only about a dozen were exceptional, so keep a Geiger counter running and expect to hit the mother lode only occasionally. _[Warren Buffett, Berkshire Hathaway]_ — [2025-03-27](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3xbhKOzNBW8)
- **Buffett's Japanese trading company bet was a no-brainer found by flipping through the Japan Company Handbook: 8% dividend yields financed by yen debt at 0.5%.** He borrowed $5 billion in yen with dividend coverage of 16x the interest, put in no equity, earned roughly 7.5% on $5B immediately, and the stocks doubled in 3-4 years with dividends now ~15% on cost; he then raised stakes toward 10% with the companies' blessing. Pabrai dog-eared Buffett's copy of the handbook around 2019. _[Mitsubishi, Marubeni, Japanese trading companies, Japan Company Handbook, Warren Buffett]_ — [2025-03-27](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3xbhKOzNBW8)
- **Never use leverage: Rick Guerin was as good as Buffett and Munger but was in a hurry, got margin calls in the 1973-74 crash and sold his Berkshire to Buffett at $40 a share.** Buffett told Pabrai and Guy Spier: 'If you are even a slightly above average investor, spend less than you earn, and use no leverage, you cannot help but get rich in a lifetime.' Rick later recovered and died worth hundreds of millions, owning most of the Daily Journal. _[Rick Guerin, Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger, Berkshire Hathaway, Daily Journal]_ — [2025-03-27](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3xbhKOzNBW8)
- **Mental models give an unfair advantage; jumpstart your latticework by rereading Munger's Psychology of Human Misjudgment every year.** The talk took Munger four or five decades to accumulate and is the last chapter of Poor Charlie's Almanack, now published cheaply in India; each rereading surfaces things he swears he is reading for the first time. _[Charlie Munger, Poor Charlie's Almanack]_ — [2025-04-22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YBinkgDRPHo)
- **Lollapalooza effects happen when multiple mental models push in the same direction, so one plus one equals eleven.** Munger's observation; his own fund launch combined the cloning model, the reciprocation model and 'what is going on here'. _[Charlie Munger]_ — [2025-04-22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YBinkgDRPHo)
- **Even Buffett's hit rate is only 2 to 4%: about a dozen truly good decisions out of 400-500 important ones in 60 years drove all of Berkshire's value.** Buffett wrote that most of his capital allocation decisions were 'so-so' and results came from about a dozen good ones, one every five years; Pabrai lists Ajit Jain (north of $100 billion of value created), See's, Coke, Apple, National Indemnity and Mid-American among them. _[Berkshire Hathaway, Ajit Jain, See's Candies, Coca-Cola, Apple, National Indemnity, Mid-American]_ — [2025-05-02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NrTz1uiL3RU)
- **The best things about Buffett and Munger have nothing to do with investing; they are about how to lead a great life.** Pabrai had dinner with Charlie four or five times a year and learned mostly by observing how he interacted with family and visitors and his everyday habits; learning only the investing side misses most of it. _[Charlie Munger, Warren Buffett]_ — [2025-05-02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NrTz1uiL3RU)
- **There is no shortcut to finding ideas: 'start with the As' and go through everything one by one, the way Buffett did with racetrack tickets, Moody's Manuals and the Japan Company Handbook.** Buffett found the five Japanese trading houses by flipping the Japan Company Handbook for more than 10 years, refusing Pabrai's efforts (via Tracy Britt) to switch him to a $10,000 Capital IQ screen; he bought 8% yielders financed entirely in yen at 0.5%, and the dividends have since doubled. _[Warren Buffett, Japanese trading houses, Moody's Manual, Japan Company Handbook, Capital IQ, Tracy Britt]_ — [2025-05-02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NrTz1uiL3RU)
- **Berkshire today is like an index fund but a better index than the S&P 500, given its large cash position, modest valuation and relatively young leader.** Greg Abel has effectively run the wholly owned businesses for a few years and nobody noticed a difference; the public portfolio passes to him within about six months. Passive investing is now over half of US investing and produces lemming behavior into Mag 7 names regardless of fundamentals. _[Berkshire Hathaway, Greg Abel, Warren Buffett]_ — [2025-06-10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jW-L5NdvYkU)

### Mistakes & lessons learned (15)

- **Frontline was a first-order-thinking mistake: he took a 70-80% gain in under a year and missed what would have been a 70-bagger in four or five years.** He focused only on the liquidation-value downside with non-recourse ship debt and did not appreciate that John Fredriksen was a gifted capital allocator or that spot rates could go to $250-300,000 a day with the whole fleet on spot. _[Frontline, John Fredriksen]_ — [2025-01-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MGqKFwtCWnU)
- **Losing $4.5 million ($2 million his own) on a dot-com startup in 1998-99 put him six to nine months ahead of the market in recognizing the bubble, which set up the fund's best years.** Pabrai Investment Funds started mid-1999 with almost no tech and a portfolio of anomalies and special situations in cheap brick-and-mortar businesses; from 1999-2007 it had no down years, mid-30s annualized before fees and high-20s after, while the Nasdaq crashed. By 2007 he managed about $600 million. _[Pabrai Investment Funds]_ — [2025-01-31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JpGi2c7a1gw)
- **The 2007-09 financial crisis, when the fund fell 65-67% versus 40% for markets, forced a rethink that led to great investments he would not otherwise have made.** He was clueless about the crash and had significant exposure to leveraged financial institutions, the worst place to be, taking a couple of 100% losses. Munger: learn from mistakes but do not learn too much; study them and move on. _[Charlie Munger, Pabrai Investment Funds]_ — [2025-01-31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JpGi2c7a1gw)
- **Start new endeavors small so failures are contained, then press the accelerator only when there is traction; the failures are what teach you.** Many of his ventures did not work; the ones that worked taught him nothing, so he cherishes failures and refuses to sweep them under the rug. — [2025-02-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HSq4QOCuuDA)
- **Selling great businesses because of valuation is one of the dumbest things you can do, and I did it repeatedly, most painfully with Ferrari.** In 2012 Fiat Chrysler had a $5-6 billion market cap and he invested $50-60 million for ~1%; that stake included 80% of Ferrari, now worth $90 billion, so doing nothing would have left a ~$900 million position against his ~$1 billion of total assets, versus the ~$150 million he captured. _[Fiat Chrysler, Ferrari]_ — [2025-02-25](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Eww63NIxKew)
- **Always ask Buffett's question 'and then what?'; first-order thinking cost him 97% of the Frontline upside because he did not think through scrapping, fleet shrinkage and the 3-4 year shipbuilding lag.** Single-hull ships were scrapped, the fleet fell from 300 to 250, and once demand returned shipyards were backlogged for five years with prices rising from $70M to $120M per ship, so rates stayed high for 1000+ days. _[Frontline]_ — [2025-03-27](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3xbhKOzNBW8)
- **His investing model was flawed for almost his whole career: buying at half of intrinsic value and selling at 90% is the dumbest thing because we don't know intrinsic value and great businesses surprise to the upside.** Buffett struggled to pay 25 million for See's Candies, yet dividends are approaching 3 billion, more than 100x the investment, which they would never have guessed. His advice to his 40-year-old self: when you own an exceptional business don't sell at 90% of intrinsic value, fully priced, or overpriced, only consider selling when egregiously overpriced. _[See's Candies]_ — [2025-04-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ePBZbS0cRAM)
- **His biggest flawed model was selling great businesses at 90% of intrinsic value to buy something half off, because intrinsic value is unknowable and great businesses are rare anomalies.** Do not sell a great business when fully priced or even overpriced; sit until valuation becomes completely egregious. He hopes for 29 more years of compounding to apply the lesson. — [2025-04-22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YBinkgDRPHo)
- **In 1995 he put $20,000 into Satyam, Kotak, Blue Dart and Sky Pack; Satyam went 140x by 2000 and he sold near the peak, then sold the others 'to clean up his books' and Kotak went 350x and Blue Dart 500x.** Of $1 million starting capital, $10,000 in Satyam became $1.4 million and the US portfolio about $13 million; Falguni Nayar at Kotak's London office opened his account and impressed him into the last-minute Kotak bet. Exceptional management can do exceptional things you cannot put an intrinsic value on. _[Satyam Computers, Kotak Mahindra, Blue Dart, Sky Pack, Falguni Nayar]_ — [2025-04-22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YBinkgDRPHo)
- **Most of his investments in South Korea and India did not work; a 50% error rate is normal and Templeton said the best analyst is wrong one in three times.** In South Korea none of the bets worked though he mostly got his money back; he could not do well there and found other places where he could. _[John Templeton]_ — [2025-05-02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NrTz1uiL3RU)
- **His whole history is selling too soon; the longest he has held anything is about 8 years, and you can do very well being sloppy as long as the sloppiness is on the side of inactivity.** Riding a stock from 10 to 100 and selling at 30 is not where the game is; the game is holding the one that goes from 10 to 500. — [2025-05-02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NrTz1uiL3RU)
- **Never count Tesla out because Elon is all in, but a 10%-sized position would be speculative; not being long Elon is probably one of his mistakes.** Quotes Munger: 'Never underestimate a man who overestimates himself.' Elon gets distracted running the government, so Tesla deserves at most a small allocation. _[Tesla, Elon Musk, Charlie Munger]_ — [2025-06-10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jW-L5NdvYkU)
- **His father's repeated bankruptcies taught him that offering gaps can be filled with no money, but leverage and over-aggressive growth destroy staying power.** His father went bankrupt eight or nine times; at 11-12 Pabrai and his brother acted as his board figuring out how to survive one more day. At 16 he watched his father cold-call gold shops in Abu Dhabi and Doha, where the fifth shop bought and orders grew over repeat visits. — [2025-07-13](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vNBluvpgphs)
- **Mistakes of omission are far worse than the zeros; selling Ferrari after its 2015-2018 spin-off cost him about a billion dollars.** In 2012 he bought Fiat Chrysler at a $5-6 billion valuation, ignoring that 80% of Ferrari was inside it. He made a couple of hundred million and sold after Ferrari listed; he owned roughly 1% of Ferrari, which now has a market cap near $100 billion. _[Ferrari, Fiat Chrysler, Ram, Jeep, Maserati]_ — [2025-07-13](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vNBluvpgphs)
- **He cloned Buffett badly for two decades by overdosing on Ben Graham and underdosing on Charlie Munger, yet even suboptimal cloning lands you in paradise.** After 31 years following Buffett, he says the first 20 were 'in the wilderness' despite being friends with Warren and Charlie; he figured it out only seven or eight years ago. _[Ben Graham, Charlie Munger, Warren Buffett]_ — [2025-10-14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fW9j-mDNVt8)

### Career, entrepreneurship & life (24)

- **His process has evolved through stronger mental models, more industry and geographic expertise, and the growth of assets from $1 million in 1995 to over $1 billion, which changes the universe he can look at.** The boom-and-bust model took 20-plus years to fully appreciate in all its nuances. — [2025-01-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MGqKFwtCWnU)
- **Starting over with $1 million he would focus almost entirely on special-situation anomalies in nooks and crannies, possibly with long-term options, that funds cannot touch.** Per Joel Greenblatt, exceptional small investors are forced to graduate out of fertile pastures as capital grows, leaving an evergreen opportunity set for the next batch; the little guy has a huge advantage. A friend with a small fund compounds over 50% a year on option bets but will have to leave that pasture within a year or two. _[Joel Greenblatt, Li Lu]_ — [2025-01-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MGqKFwtCWnU)
- **Investing knowledge is cumulative, so unlike a basketball player who peaks in his early thirties, an investor keeps improving as long as the top nine or twelve inches of the body work.** Munger said Warren was still getting better in his nineties; winners teach little, mistakes teach a lot. _[Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger]_ — [2025-01-31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JpGi2c7a1gw)

Life has no grand meaning, so make the most of a short time and have the most fun. _[Dakshana Foundation, Pabrai Investment Funds]_ — [2025-02-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HSq4QOCuuDA)
- **Hanging out with people better than you trumps loyalty: be a harsh grader of humans and deliberately increase time with the exceptional ones.** There is a gravitational pull both ways; he does a post-mortem after every lunch or tea to decide whether to repeat it and winnows down to people he truly enjoys. _[Warren Buffett]_ — [2025-02-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HSq4QOCuuDA)
- **Less is more: he and Buffett refuse multiple homes, and he benchmarks every activity or meeting on whether it will make him happier.** Media and advertising tell people to want bigger homes and better cars; he feels on vacation every day and often finds trips worse than daily life. He lined up $70K in unused credit-card limits and $30K in a 401k, learned personal bankruptcy would wipe the debt, and his bosses promised to rehire him 'when it fails'; both later invested in his fund. _[TransTech]_ — [2025-02-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HSq4QOCuuDA)

### Philanthropy & Dakshana (14)

- **Knowing your expected death date, June 11, 2054, frames the two games he plays: a compounding engine and a give-away engine so that only $10,000 is left the day before he dies.** He used MetLife's life-expectancy calculator. He could have retired at 33; all wealth since is abstract and will go back to society, echoing Buffett's view that 99.999% of his wealth cannot make him happier. Dakshana, 16-17 years old, must scale to give effectively. _[Dakshana Foundation, Warren Buffett, MetLife]_ — [2025-02-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HSq4QOCuuDA)
- **Dakshana's aim is the highest social return on invested capital, currently about $3,000 per student on a ~$3 million annual budget for ~1,000 kids a year.** He knows of no non-profit anywhere delivering a higher social ROIC, but the program cannot absorb more than $6-7 million a year, so at $10-30 million a year he will have to lower the bar and consider other areas such as environment or health. _[Dakshana]_ — [2025-02-25](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Eww63NIxKew)
- **Compounding and Dakshana are two math games joined at the hip: one maximizes net worth, the other gives it all away, and played perfectly there should be about $10,000 left the day before I die.** With just under 30 years of compounding left (MetLife's calculator moved his expected death from 2044 to 2054), the challenge will be on the give-back side as the numbers get larger, not on the compounding side. _[Dakshana]_ — [2025-02-25](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Eww63NIxKew)
- **Dakshana is a math game focused on social return on invested capital: about $3,000 per kid takes a family from $60 a month to Google salaries via IIT admission.** Cloned in 2006 from a man in Bihar coaching 30 poor kids for $800 each who refused to scale; Dakshana now does 1,000 kids a year heading to 2,500, spends $3-4 million a year, and its IIT admit rate rose from 8% in year one to 70% versus a 1.3% general rate. Buffett wrote him a letter calling it the best philanthropy he had seen. _[Dakshana Foundation, IIT, Warren Buffett]_ — [2025-03-27](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3xbhKOzNBW8)
- **He plans to die on June 11, 2054 with $10,000 left, because large inheritances do more harm than good and surplus compounding should be recycled at high social returns.** Quotes Buffett: give kids enough to do anything but not enough to do nothing. The giving curve must become dominant in the next few years, with $3 million a year rising to $5, 10, 15 million. _[Warren Buffett, Dakshana Foundation]_ — [2025-03-27](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3xbhKOzNBW8)
- **Dakshana is a math game: compound wealth at 15% for 29 more years (about six doubles, 64x) and give it all away so that on June 10, 2054 he has $10,000 or less left, judged fantastic by a critical observer.** If 3 billion remains a day before he dies he has lost the game. Giving to the Red Cross would be suboptimal; the challenge is quality. He admires Chuck Feeney (The Billionaire Who Wasn't), who died with little money in a rented San Francisco apartment. As numbers grow, giving money away is harder than making it. _[Dakshana Foundation, Chuck Feeney]_ — [2025-04-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ePBZbS0cRAM)
- **Dakshana's current program spends about 3 million a year and caps out around 7 million because it runs out of seats and brains, so deploying 100 million a year well is the unsolved problem of his life.** The compounding side is on autopilot; the giving side is where the challenge lies. If the extra 93 million doesn't go into endeavors that critics call awesome, that is terrible. _[Dakshana Foundation]_ — [2025-04-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ePBZbS0cRAM)
- **Because Dakshana's coaching is better than what the private sector offers, wealthy families try to crash the gate, so verifying below-poverty-line status is a constant battle handled with in-person interviews and treated like retail shrinkage.** People offer $50,000 donations for a single seat, more than private coaching costs. Dakshana targets the absolute bottom of society, tracks the percentage of wrongly supported kids as a metric, and aims to be slightly better on 20 variables each year, which compounds into world-class; Walmart's greeter is the analogy for policies that cut shrink. _[Dakshana Foundation, Walmart]_ — [2025-04-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ePBZbS0cRAM)
- **Dakshana separates church and state: faculty who teach have no say in admissions, and the admissions team is not paid on results, so incentives can't corrupt selection.** Teams are well incentivized even though many joined for the calling; the CEO and Pabrai watch both sides. Selection quality (brilliance plus poverty) drives most of the success. _[Dakshana Foundation]_ — [2025-04-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ePBZbS0cRAM)
- **It is impossible to optimize for more than one or two variables; Dakshana selects only on brilliance and socioeconomic status and keeps the game plan simple enough for everyone to understand.** Adding criteria like abusive households would make the problem too complicated; if you want to help abused kids, don't restrict to brilliant abused kids. More than half of Dakshana's hires are now alumni (oldest are 33-34), who make up everything below the CEO and whose passion for the mission vastly exceeds his. _[Dakshana Foundation]_ — [2025-04-15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ePBZbS0cRAM)
- **Dakshana is a cloned model, scaled from a Bihar math teacher's 30 students a year to 1,000, spending about $3,000 per student to get poor kids into IIT.** He read about the teacher in BusinessWeek in 2006; the teacher got 90%+ of very poor students into IIT versus a sub-1% national admit rate (2 million test-takers for ~16,000 seats) but had no interest in scaling, so Pabrai asked to clone it. $3,000 moves a family from $1,000-2,000 a year to $100,000-200,000 via jobs at Google or Microsoft. _[Dakshana, IIT, Anand Kumar]_ — [2025-10-14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fW9j-mDNVt8)
- **Dakshana works because it leverages two free government systems, the IITs and the JNV magnet schools, giving a 60-to-1 or 70-to-1 subsidy on its spending.** The IITs spend $50-60,000 a year per student and JNVs another $15-20,000, close to $250,000 per child in total, against Dakshana's $3,000. IIT Bombay Computer Science, which closes by rank 80, has more brainpower than any classroom at MIT or Stanford; Bill Gates said he would recruit only from IITs if limited to one school. _[Dakshana, IIT, JNV, Bill Gates]_ — [2025-10-14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fW9j-mDNVt8)
- **Dakshana's medical track now places 25% of its students into AIIMS, which has a 0.1% admit rate, a 250x higher hit rate than the general population.** Those who miss AIIMS get into other government medical colleges; AIIMS alumni like Deepak Chopra are among the best doctors in the world. _[Dakshana, AIIMS, Deepak Chopra]_ — [2025-10-14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fW9j-mDNVt8)
- **His goal since 2006-07 is to be remembered for Dakshana rather than as an investor, and his daughter's Dakshana tattoo is his highest accomplishment as a dad.** He says the goal is already largely met with about 30 years still to go. _[Dakshana]_ — [2025-10-14](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fW9j-mDNVt8)

### Cloning & learning from great investors (8)

- **Be a shameless cloner: the world can accommodate multiples of the same thing, and Walmart and Microsoft were built entirely on copied ideas.** Sam Walton visited more non-Walmart stores than any human and learned from a badly run store's candle display. Microsoft took Word from WordPerfect, Excel from Lotus, Windows from the Mac and bought MS-DOS; even its AI comes from outside. A Starbucks does not preclude another coffee shop. _[Walmart, Sam Walton, Microsoft, Starbucks]_ — [2026-03-16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6QGCPDTZDB8)
- **Listening to David Senra's Founders Podcast episode on a book extracts more than reading the book yourself in a fraction of the time, so he is going all in on every episode.** He listens at least an hour a day, has done about 270 of 400+ episodes working backward to September 2020, and expects to finish in 6-10 months. Listening to every episode regardless of subject introduces randomness, which Munger championed. He also likes Business Breakdowns and Acquired. _[David Senra, The Founders Podcast, Charlie Munger]_ — [2026-03-16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6QGCPDTZDB8)
- **Pulak Prasad's 'What I Learned About Investing From Darwin' is one of the best investment books he has read, and Prasad's Nalanda model of years of research then permanent ownership is a wonderful framework.** Prasad runs about $5 billion from Singapore, is closed to new capital, posts his whole portfolio on the homepage with no movement, and treats well-run basic businesses with exceptional governance as marriages. _[Pulak Prasad, Nalanda Capital]_ — [2026-03-23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b3gPwuMs9xc)
- **Be a shameless cloner: not one idea in his portfolio is his own, and you would do extremely well limited to Value Investors Club write-ups, even just letters A through H.** VIC was set up by Joel Greenblatt; DataRoma shows quarterly what the luminaries bought and sold. His latest cloned idea is Gimat Gross, 'Turkey's Costco'. _[Value Investors Club, Joel Greenblatt, DataRoma, Gimat Gross]_ — [2026-04-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iir-07rEf5o)
- **He is the shameless cloner: everything in his portfolio came from someone else, and it is dangerous to come up with investment ideas on your own.** Value Investors Club is free and its stringent membership means above-average ideas; he reads its write-up first on any business, and has his assistant print the first two pages of all new VIC ideas every couple of months. DataRoma and SumZero are other sources; his latest cloned idea is 'Turkey's Costco'. One to three ideas a year is enough. _[Value Investors Club, DataRoma, SumZero, Turkey's Costco]_ — [2026-05-01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yx1yAhjsDsE)
- **Humans are terrible at cloning, which is why cloning works: everyone knows exactly what Elon or Walmart did and still will not copy it.** Sam Walton had no original ideas: Walmart came from Kmart, Sam's Club from Sol Price's Price Club; he stopped the car on family vacations to tour competitors' stores and brought donuts to truck drivers at 5:30am to learn what they saw. Burger King's site-selection model was two guys putting stores across the street from McDonald's. Elon Musk's 'idiot index' (a $5,000 part with $270 of raw materials made in-house for $500) is known to Boeing and every carmaker, yet none adopt it because it is not in their DNA. _[Sam Walton, Walmart, Sol Price, Costco, Burger King, McDonald's, Tesla, SpaceX, Boeing, Elon Musk]_ — [2026-05-05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m8jNKvcXolE)
- **'Take a simple idea and take it seriously' is the bedrock model without which cloning or any other model works; you have to go all in.** Once he saw Turkey was absurdly cheap he chose to be an inch wide and a mile deep, treating the Turkish market as his Moody's Manual and studying every company. Using several models together yields Munger's lollapalooza effect (1+1 becomes 11); the models do the heavy lifting and all you have to do is not violate them. _[Charlie Munger]_ — [2026-05-05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m8jNKvcXolE)
- **Finding ideas is easy: read every write-up on Value Investors Club until one hits you over the head with a 2x4.** VIC is free with a 60-day delay, which is irrelevant; a write-up hands you the company and the person on a platter. When someone told Buffett there are 5,000 US stocks he said 'start with the A's'. If it is your deepest desire it is not work, it is like watching World Cup highlights. _[Value Investors Club, Kaspi, Warren Buffett]_ — [2026-07-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YQq0A1haFo4)

### Circle of competence & checklists (15)

- **The size of the circle of competence is irrelevant; be an inch wide and a mile deep at its epicenter.** John Arrillaga became a billionaire investing only in real estate within one mile of Stanford, knowing 50 years of rents on every building, staying under-levered and buying marquee properties in crises. _[John Arrillaga, Marc Andreessen]_ — [2026-04-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iir-07rEf5o)
- **If you cannot explain the thesis to a 10-year-old in three or four sentences, do not invest; and delete Excel, because if you cannot do the math quickly in your head it is a pass.** He told Columbia students that the program makes them overdose on Excel and that his only use of it was the deep-well rope. — [2026-04-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iir-07rEf5o)
- **A 213-question pre-investment checklist built from great investors' mistakes shows the three big failure causes are leverage, misunderstood moats and leadership or ownership problems.** He studied why Buffett lost money on Dexter Shoes. Do not buy levered businesses and make sure you understand the business well. _[Dexter Shoes, Warren Buffett]_ — [2026-04-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iir-07rEf5o)
- **The size of your circle of competence is irrelevant; staying in its epicenter is what matters.** John Arrillaga, Munger's friend, became a billionaire from nothing investing only in real estate within a mile of Stanford, knowing the history of every building and buying underlevered properties during distress. Within your circle, intrinsic value should be obvious; if it is not obvious you are outside your circle. _[John Arrillaga, Marc Andreessen]_ — [2026-05-01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yx1yAhjsDsE)
- **If you cannot explain the thesis to a 10-year-old in four sentences and do the math in your head, take a pass.** A 10-year-old will not understand an Excel spreadsheet; the four sentences should not need many numbers. The only exception is when you are in a deep well and need a rope. — [2026-05-01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yx1yAhjsDsE)
- **Use a pre-investment checklist built from the mistakes of great investors; the three biggest failure causes are leverage, misjudged moats and questionable leadership or ownership.** He started the checklist about 15 years ago with 70-80 questions and it now has about 213. Berkshire's Dexter Shoes, bought with 2% of Berkshire stock, went to zero because of cheap offshore manufacturing, generating the question 'could this business be hurt by cheaper offshore manufacturing?'. _[Dexter Shoes, Berkshire Hathaway]_ — [2026-05-01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yx1yAhjsDsE)
- **'Thou shalt not use Excel', and if you cannot explain the thesis to a 10-year-old in four sentences, it is a pass; 98% of businesses belong in the too-hard pile.** Every investment starts complex but must reduce to four simple sentences. With 50,000 stocks in the world, 98% belong in Buffett's 'too hard' box; sorting honestly is an exercise in humility and the inner scorecard. GLP-1 drugs (Wegovy, then Mounjaro, now tablets) and Bitcoin both go in the too-hard pile: rapid change is the enemy of the investor, and given gold, 'why do we need Bitcoin?' _[Warren Buffett, Wegovy, Mounjaro, Bitcoin]_ — [2026-05-05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m8jNKvcXolE)
- **The checklist copies the FAA: changes are only made after a crash, and a stock that went to zero is a crash with no survivors while a stock sold at a loss is a crash with some survivors.** The FAA values a life at about $5 million and mandates fixes only when cheaper than expected losses, which makes flying both safe and cheap; he studied the mistakes of great investors, such as Buffett paying 2% of Berkshire for Dexter, which was killed by cheap foreign competition, and turned each into a question. _[FAA, Dexter Shoe, Berkshire Hathaway, Shimano, Korean Air]_ — [2026-06-08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NVD-m9seDe4)
- **The checklist started 16-17 years ago with 70-80 questions, now has 213, takes 1-2 hours to run, and he runs it every time before buying since he makes only 2-3 investments a year.** The first pass reveals questions he cannot answer, which means the work is not done; then he examines the failures and decides whether to 'take off'. On critics: 'if they can criticize Gandhi, then I am fair game.' _[Warren Buffett, Gandhi]_ — [2026-05-05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m8jNKvcXolE)
- **Risk-free investments are found only in sectors that are hated and unloved; when everything is loved, do not buy.** Investing is about anomalies, things that make no sense, like a power company at 3 times earnings; most people ignore boring businesses because they seek excitement. — [2026-06-08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NVD-m9seDe4)
- **Your deepest desire is your destiny — you can have only one, and if it is to find stocks at a P/E of one among 50,000 stocks, you will find them.** Quoting the Upanishads: buy in hook, line and sinker, have a singular focus and go all in like Bezos with the world's largest bookstore or Elon wanting to die on Mars. It is important to have the right desires and not blow it with stupid ones. _[Jeff Bezos, Elon Musk, Amazon]_ — [2026-07-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YQq0A1haFo4)
- **There are no called strikes in investing — never invest in Turkey or anywhere else until you are 5,000% all in; if you harbor doubts, move on.** Buffett can let 10,000 pitches go by and swings only when the ball looks like a watermelon; you may see Kaspi as a tiny marble in the corner of your strike zone and that is fine. This is a forgiving business and you need not own what Pabrai or Buffett owns. _[Warren Buffett, Kaspi, Turkey]_ — [2026-07-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YQq0A1haFo4)
- **Focus is the single most important mental model — be all in on one little thing and life will be amazing.** Deepest desire is another way of describing focus; you cannot have ten desires. — [2026-07-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YQq0A1haFo4)
- **Turkey is a market of gamblers who buy at 10 and sell at 3 hoping for 10%, which lets a patient buyer accumulate a third of a company; the stock market transfers wealth from the active to the inactive.** The average Turkish public company cycles through its float every 17 days; Buffett's quote on the active and inactive explains why the volume made a 33% stake possible. _[Turkey, Reysas, Warren Buffett]_ — [2026-08-25](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f4tMPhZAI5E)

### Buffett & Munger lessons (18)

- **Mental models are truths that surprise you when first encountered, and cascading them in the same direction produces Munger's lollapalooza effect where 1 plus 1 becomes 11.** He rereads Munger's Psychology of Human Misjudgment in Poor Charlie's Almanack every year and says it took him decades to understand; combining models is the single model with the biggest impact on his life. _[Charlie Munger, Poor Charlie's Almanack]_ — [2026-03-16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6QGCPDTZDB8)
- **Poor Charlie's Almanack, Cialdini's work and Kevin Kelly's recent book teach more than any college degree, and the best things in life are free.** Robert Cialdini is a good friend; he discovered Kevin Kelly's book through The Founders Podcast. _[Robert Cialdini, Kevin Kelly, Poor Charlie's Almanack]_ — [2026-03-16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6QGCPDTZDB8)
- **Greg Abel occupies a middle ground between Buffett's delegation-to-abdication and being overbearing, and Berkshire's long-undermanaged subsidiaries will now see tighter operations.** Munger said Greg is better than Warren in some important ways; Greg runs 80-plus businesses from Des Moines with a team of about 30 between him and the subsidiaries, and will act when a manager isn't delivering. Munger agreed with Pabrai that the furniture and jewelry retailers bought after Nebraska Furniture Mart and Borsheims were 'useless'. _[Berkshire Hathaway, Greg Abel, Charlie Munger, Nebraska Furniture Mart, Borsheims]_ — [2026-03-23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b3gPwuMs9xc)
- **Munger bought CONSOL in May 2023 within two weeks of Pabrai without either speaking to the other, said 'it was bound to happen', and after reading Pabrai's write-up was still buying Alpha six days before he died at 99.9.** In October 2023, for the first time in their friendship, Pabrai asked to meet Charlie and flew from Austin for what became their last meal four weeks before his death. Munger's life expectancy was irrelevant to him; he was still excited to make bets. _[Charlie Munger, CONSOL Energy, Alpha Metallurgical Resources]_ — [2026-03-23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b3gPwuMs9xc)
- **Mental models must be adopted cult-like with full immersion; the bedrock model is 'take a simple idea and take it seriously', and if you have even a hundredth of a percent of doubt you are better off not touching it.** Human brains evolved to see a distorted reality; 'aha' moments where the world works differently than you thought are the models that give an edge. Overlaying models yields Munger's Lollapalooza effect where 1 plus 1 becomes 11. _[Charlie Munger, Poor Charlie's Almanack]_ — [2026-04-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iir-07rEf5o)
- **Read the footnotes, turn every page, and enjoy hunting for needles in haystacks as Buffett has done from age 12 to 95.** Buffett collected discarded racetrack tickets at Aksarben at 12, found Western Insurance at $15 with $25 earnings in Moody's Manual at 23, and after 15-20 years reading the Japan Company Handbook bought five trading companies at 7-8% yields fully funded with yen borrowed at 0.5%; dividends doubled and stocks tripled. Seth Klarman named a horse 'Read the Footnotes'; Robert Caro, the best researcher and writer, turns every page of 50 million at the LBJ Library. _[Warren Buffett, Western Insurance, Japanese trading companies, Seth Klarman, Robert Caro]_ — [2026-04-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iir-07rEf5o)
- **Always have someone you trust to discuss investment ideas with, because your brain will convince you a bad idea is the best thing since sliced bread.** Munger said it was not always Warren; he ordered Pabrai and Li Lu to lunch at least monthly, which they did at Din Tai Fung. Guy Spier serves the same role. _[Charlie Munger, Li Lu, Guy Spier]_ — [2026-04-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iir-07rEf5o)
- **The bedrock mental model is Munger's 'take a simple idea and take it seriously'; none of the other models work unless you go all in on this one, and it is the one most people understand but fail to follow.** Overlaying models on each other produces Munger's Lollapalooza Effect where 1 plus 1 becomes 11. People think the idea is too simple; you have to take deliberate, fanatical action, which pushes you to one extreme and can be uncomfortable. _[Charlie Munger, Poor Charlie's Almanack]_ — [2026-05-01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yx1yAhjsDsE)
- **Read the footnotes and turn every page; enjoy hunting for needles in haystacks as Buffett did from the Aksarben racetrack to the Moody's Manuals to the Japan Company Handbook.** At 12 Buffett collected discarded winning tickets at Aksarben; at 24 he found Western Insurance at $15 with $25 of earnings in Moody's (would have compounded ~19% for 70 years); in his 80s he found the five Japanese trading companies in the Japan Company Handbook, putting $5 billion in, 100% borrowed in yen at 0.5% against 8% dividends, since doubled to $10 billion with almost $1 billion a year in dividends. Seth Klarman named horses 'Read the Footnotes' and 'Margin of Safety'; Robert Caro is the best researcher and writer ever. _[Warren Buffett, Western Insurance, Japanese trading companies, Seth Klarman, Robert Caro, Greg Abel]_ — [2026-05-01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yx1yAhjsDsE)
- **Always have someone to discuss investment ideas with, because the brain is a dangerous place.** Charlie Munger told him it was not always Warren, but he always had someone to talk to; in 2009 Munger told him and Li Lu to meet monthly, which they did at Din Tai Fung in Arcadia. A VIC idea passes one brain filter, yours is the second, and a trusted third person is powerful. _[Charlie Munger, Li Lu, Guy Spier, Value Investors Club]_ — [2026-05-01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yx1yAhjsDsE)
- **Buffett's American Express salad-oil bet shows scuttlebutt beats spreadsheets: he checked whether the moat (brand trust) was intact by standing at Omaha restaurant cash registers.** After the salad-oil fraud (warehouses of seawater) crushed the stock, Buffett saw zero merchant hesitation to accept the card and put 40% of his fund into Amex. He similarly went to see Snow White with a briefcase to study Disney, of which he owned ~5%; he sold both at a profit but holding them 20-30 years would have done far better. _[American Express, Disney, Warren Buffett]_ — [2026-05-05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m8jNKvcXolE)
- **If you are even slightly above average, spend less than you earn and never use leverage, you cannot help but get rich over a lifetime.** From his 2007 $650,000 lunch with Buffett: Rick Guerin, the third partner, was always on margin, got margin calls in the 1973-74 crash and sold his Berkshire shares to Buffett at $40 (now over $700,000). 'Charlie and I always knew we were going to be rich, but we were not in a hurry.' _[Rick Guerin, Warren Buffett, Berkshire Hathaway]_ — [2026-05-05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m8jNKvcXolE)
- **Berkshire's $380 billion cash pile will likely be halved or less within 5 years as dislocations bring the desperate 'Saturday phone calls'.** Berkshire is now run by a great operator and pretty good capital allocator rather than a great capital allocator, but Greg Abel will get the weekend calls in a crisis. Investing requires extreme patience with extreme decisiveness, like Munger standing by a stream with a spear waiting for the salmon. _[Berkshire Hathaway, Greg Abel, Charlie Munger]_ — [2026-05-05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m8jNKvcXolE)
- **The $650,000 Buffett lunch was one of the best deals ever, a tuition bill for the $70 million he had already made from Buffett's ideas, that turned into infinite free lunches and friendships.** He had budgeted $2 million (about 3% of his gains) and Guy Spier capped at $250,000; Buffett studied everyone's bios, set no time limit, then competitively set up a lunch with Charlie that led to dinners every 3-4 months and bridge at the LA Country Club, plus yearly invitations to Buffett's private Sunday brunch. By contrast, a charity lunch with Google CEO Eric Schmidt ended at 1 hour 1 minute and rated 2 out of 10. _[Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger, Guy Spier, Eric Schmidt, Google]_ — [2026-06-08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NVD-m9seDe4)
- **Berkshire's constraint is size, not Greg Abel versus Warren Buffett — with a trillion dollars even Buffett has his hands tied.** Give Greg Abel $1 billion or even $50 billion and he would be killing it; Berkshire should not distribute its $400 billion cash because a big dislocation in the next 5-10 years could absorb all of it. _[Berkshire Hathaway, Greg Abel, Warren Buffett]_ — [2026-07-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YQq0A1haFo4)
- **Buffett's ~$30 billion Google bet makes sense because his universe is tiny — if he managed $100 billion there would be no Google bet.** Buffett has studied Google for years: GEICO paid $20 a click that cost Google under a cent, and Sergey and Larry visited him before the IPO to learn how to run a company like Berkshire. Berkshire generates $50-60 billion of cash flow a year and Google is a $4 trillion company. _[Google, Alphabet, Berkshire Hathaway, GEICO, Warren Buffett]_ — [2026-07-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YQq0A1haFo4)
- **Munger's rule: you get a few trips to the pie counter in a lifetime, so load up and don't drop the pie; don't worry about getting good at selling, worry about getting good at finding Costcos.** You can be useless at selling and have a high error rate as long as you recognize the truly exceptional holding and don't sell it when it looks fully priced or overpriced, only possibly when egregiously overpriced. _[Charlie Munger, Costco]_ — [2026-08-25](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f4tMPhZAI5E)
- **Most of what he learned from Munger came from observing how he lived rather than what he said, including a frugality that was calibrated, not reflexive.** Munger wore a belt worn out 10-15 years earlier and $10 Costco flannel shirts and happily flew Southwest middle seats, yet paid $80,000 for a NetJets flight home from Costa Rica when he had a bad headache; the vast public body of work means you can learn from Buffett and Munger without ever meeting them. _[Charlie Munger, Costco, NetJets, Southwest Airlines]_ — [2026-08-25](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f4tMPhZAI5E)

### Mistakes & lessons learned (4)

- **Frontline in 2002 was a stock with no downside where he doubled, patted himself on the back, exited, and then watched it go up 200x.** A 2025 offshore-driller conference field trip to Frontline's ornate harbor-front Oslo headquarters, full of VLCC replicas and art, felt like God rubbing his nose in it: he once owned 2% of all that, paid for by a rounding error of the returns. He also recounts visiting Michael Burry in September 2008 and having CDSs go over his head. _[Frontline, John Fredriksen, Michael Burry]_ — [2026-03-23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b3gPwuMs9xc)
- **His most painful mistakes are great businesses he sold: nearly 1% of Ferrari bought for about $10 million, Progressive 25 years ago, and Goldman Sachs at $65 in the crisis.** He paid an effective market cap under $1 billion for Ferrari; Buffett bought Goldman at $130 and Pabrai at half that, then sold for a good profit when he should never have sold. Even five years ago he did not understand these models. _[Ferrari, Progressive, Goldman Sachs]_ — [2026-04-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iir-07rEf5o)
- **The mistakes that hurt most are not the zeros but the great businesses you sold and should not have; go to the pie counter rarely, load up, and do not drop the pie on the way back.** He dropped Ferrari, Progressive and Goldman Sachs. He and a shareholder both sold Micron at a double from $30 in 2017-18; it is now near $600, but he does not count it as a regret because AI was not foreseeable. 99% of ideas, including Nvidia and Amazon if not obvious to you, belong in Buffett's 'too hard' box. _[Ferrari, Progressive, Goldman Sachs, Micron, Nvidia, Amazon]_ — [2026-05-01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yx1yAhjsDsE)
- **I was overdosed on Graham and underdosed on Fisher and Munger — if starting over I would go 20% Graham, 80% Fisher-Munger.** The realization came only seven or eight years ago after 32 years of investing; for almost a quarter century he was 'wandering in the wilderness, aimlessly misdirected'. _[Ben Graham, Philip Fisher, Charlie Munger]_ — [2026-07-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YQq0A1haFo4)

### Career, entrepreneurship & life (23)

- **Your deepest desire is your destiny: if you truly want something and go all in, the world reconfigures around you regardless of your expertise.** He cites Marc Andreessen's 'the world is a very malleable place' and the Upanishads' 'as is your desire, so is your will... so is your destiny', plus David Senra's 'belief comes before capability', which applied to Ford, Microsoft and his own blackjack system. _[Marc Andreessen, David Senra, Ford, Microsoft]_ — [2026-03-16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6QGCPDTZDB8)
- **Structure every venture as heads I win, tails I don't lose much, because business allows asymmetric bets of 1,000 or 10,000 runs rather than baseball's four.** Per Jeff Bezos on asymmetric bets. More than 99% of businesses worldwide are started for under $10,000 and Walmart and IKEA started with nothing, so don't waste time raising money; without capital in, there is no downside. _[Jeff Bezos, Walmart, IKEA]_ — [2026-03-16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6QGCPDTZDB8)
- **Don't quit your job to start a business; drop to just above firing level and put the other 40-50 of the week's 168 hours into the venture at zero cost.** Once the venture gets traction you switch over, and if it fails you return to square one with a new idea. His own success came on the third venture; he never quit until that one worked. — [2026-03-16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6QGCPDTZDB8)
- **The purpose of business is to deliver a great product or service to humanity, not to make money; start just to get rich and you won't.** If you serve humanity in a great way there is a basis to get rich and the journey is fun; the money follows. — [2026-03-16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6QGCPDTZDB8)
- **Put a value on your own time and delegate everything that can be done for less; he valued his time at $50-100 an hour at his first company and a few thousand an hour today.** Almost anything can be done by someone else for under $100 an hour, certainly for a few hundred, so he works only on things he is intensely excited about and lets his team handle the rest. — [2026-03-16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6QGCPDTZDB8)
- **Your startup idea won't work as conceived because it came from the ivory tower between your ears; customers will tell you the real pain point if you listen.** A Chicago bank CIO kept forcing him back to slide 10; he expanded that one slide into a 20-slide deck, dropped the rest, and got a purchase order 15 minutes after the next presentation because it became a laser-guided missile on everyone's pain point. — [2026-03-16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6QGCPDTZDB8)
- **These models apply more to coffee shops and yoga studios than to tech startups, since 99.9% of the million-plus US businesses started each year are not venture-backed.** The media over-covers venture-backed startups; he is not a tech guy. — [2026-03-16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6QGCPDTZDB8)
- **Intensity and structured daily work apply in creative fields too: Seinfeld writes on a yellow pad for 1.5-2 hours daily and Charles Schulz worked eight hours a day.** He recommends Seinfeld's Is This Anything? and Founders Podcast episodes on musicians and artists such as Jay-Z, who researched every artist before him. _[Jerry Seinfeld, Larry David, Charles Schulz, Jay-Z]_ — [2026-03-16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6QGCPDTZDB8)
- **The models are about happiness more than success; he focuses on happiness, and hard choices about people make life happier.** He admits he has vices and sometimes self-sabotages. At nearly 62 he says hearing this talk at 18 would have been a huge advantage. — [2026-03-16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6QGCPDTZDB8)
- **He has delegated to the point of abdication and refuses to spend brain cells on reviews or compensation, structuring life around what he loves and handing the rest to a few gifted people.** He has never filled out the firm's 360-review software, sending a few sentences and 'warm regards' instead. He advises figuring out what you love, what you don't, and who else can do what you don't. — [2026-03-23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b3gPwuMs9xc)
- **He launched the Pabrai Wagons ETF because Pabrai Investment Funds' multi-million minimums serve only a small sliver, and he wanted a way to serve 'Joe Public' around the world without being elitist.** The funds are over $1 billion and concentrated; ETF rules force far more diversification than his natural bent, but a spectacular winner takes care of itself even from a small position as long as you never trim. _[Pabrai Wagons ETF, Pabrai Investment Funds]_ — [2026-03-23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b3gPwuMs9xc)
- **His bond with Guy Spier, his best friend despite their differences, comes down to 'I see you': each understands what the other needs in a way almost no one else does.** On a 17-hour Rajdhani Express trip from Mumbai to Delhi he told Guy to tip the butler $25 up front, after which Guy rang the bell 30 times for tea and was ecstatic; he recently wrote Guy an old-fashioned letter about this. _[Guy Spier]_ — [2026-03-23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b3gPwuMs9xc)
- **Who we are is hard-coded by age 5, so parents should focus for the first six years, coach from 6 to 12, and after 12 control only who the child's friends are.** After 12 children are influenced by friends; when a low-quality friend appears, make a major insertion and remove that friend regardless of collateral damage. Buffett at 95 is the same kid he was at 12. _[Warren Buffett]_ — [2026-04-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iir-07rEf5o)
- **Introduce randomness into your life; picking up a Peter Lynch book at a London airport in 1994 led him to Buffett and to starting a fund.** He had never bought a stock; Lynch's reverential references sent him to the Berkshire letters and Buffett biographies. Munger told him many times to introduce randomness. _[Peter Lynch, Charlie Munger, Warren Buffett]_ — [2026-04-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iir-07rEf5o)
- **He never talks to his kids about investing, but his daughter is already interested only in great businesses, though she pays too much.** The apple falls directly under the tree; her favorite or second-favorite stock is Turkish Costco. _[Gimat Gross]_ — [2026-04-21](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iir-07rEf5o)
- **Introduce randomness into your life: reading One Up on Wall Street by chance in 1994 and going to Omaha in 1997 changed his career.** Munger sought out new people for randomness. Pabrai listens to every Founders podcast episode backward (at 115 of about 415) precisely because he does not get to pick the books. _[Peter Lynch, Charlie Munger, Founders podcast, David Senra]_ — [2026-05-01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yx1yAhjsDsE)
- **Small capital is an evergreen advantage because good investors are forced to abandon small ponds as their assets grow; pursue what you are most excited about, not what looks like it will be hot.** Buffett must deploy tens of billions at a time in a limited number of places. Family-controlled public companies like Walmart (family still owns over 40% after 50-plus years) are a universe that generally beats the whole market; the best course for most companies is never to go public. _[Walmart, Warren Buffett, John Arrillaga]_ — [2026-05-01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yx1yAhjsDsE)
- **Introduce randomness into your life and hang out with people better than you; that is how your circle of competence naturally expands.** Picking up Peter Lynch's One Up on Wall Street at Heathrow in 1994 led him to Buffett, the Berkshire letters, the 1997 annual meeting, Munger's bridge table and his best friendships; Charlie told him 'introduce randomness in your life', and the 2018 Turkey trip was the same idea. There is a gravitational pull toward the people you spend time with, and you only need a few such relationships. _[Peter Lynch, Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger]_ — [2026-05-05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m8jNKvcXolE)
- **Do not die at 25 and get buried at 75: keep growing and making bets as if you were 25, as Munger did, buying a stock six days before he died at 99.9.** Ben Franklin's quote; Munger ignored his mortality when making decisions. Gandhi: 'live as if you were to die tomorrow, learn as if you were to live forever.' Deferring life for a McKinsey stint is, per Buffett, like saving sex for old age. Ken Griffin rejected a recruit who would quit after making $10 million because 'we do not want someone who dies at 25'. _[Charlie Munger, Ben Franklin, Gandhi, Ken Griffin]_ — [2026-05-05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m8jNKvcXolE)
- **The most important thing in life is not being a great investor but leading an aligned life: discovering your calling, which is hardcoded by age five, and getting your music out.** He found his calling at 34-35 through industrial psychologists (Jack Skeen), having wandered 'in the wilderness' before that; the shortcut is psychological testing, otherwise track what energizes you. The brain is set to specialize from 11 to 20, exactly when school makes you a jack of all trades; Gates got 20,000 coding hours by his early 20s, and a parent's job is to maximize time on what an 11-12 year old is good at. _[Jack Skeen, Bill Gates, Guy Spier]_ — [2026-05-05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m8jNKvcXolE)
- **The surest way to build wealth is two boring things: spend less than you earn, and put the savings into something hated and unloved like Berkshire or an index, set it and forget it, and keep adding every month for 50 years.** A 22-year-old saving 15% of a $50,000 salary ($5,000-7,000 a year) whose pay rises to $250,000 will have 'too much' money at 72; get your excitement from other places in life, not the stock market. _[Berkshire Hathaway]_ — [2026-06-08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NVD-m9seDe4)
- **If wealth is lost, nothing is lost; if health is lost, something is lost; if character is lost, everything is lost.** His closing advice: do not worry about wealth, worry a little about health, and worry a lot about character. — [2026-06-08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NVD-m9seDe4)
- **Before managing other people's money, build an auditable 5-10 year track record in a dedicated brokerage account, then raise from friends, family and fools.** The account should be one that an audit firm can later verify; the most important source of early capital is the fools. — [2026-08-25](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f4tMPhZAI5E)

### Philanthropy & Dakshana (2)

- **Giving money away is harder than making it, and Dakshana's engine will max out at $6-7 million a year from about $3 million today.** The remaining problems are ones many smart well-resourced people have failed to solve, and headwinds grow with size. He is skeptical of Buffett's requirement that all three children agree on gifts because committees are not good at anything. _[Dakshana, Warren Buffett]_ — [2026-05-01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yx1yAhjsDsE)
- **He invests because he is wired to play single-player games; he runs a compounding engine and a give-back engine (Dakshana) and wants to have $10,000 left the day before he dies.** Personality is baked by age five; he jokes that 'God Google' told him he will die June 11, 2054, so the giving curve must accelerate as compounding continues, with Dakshana generating very high returns for society. _[Dakshana Foundation]_ — [2026-06-08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NVD-m9seDe4)
